author: oserhan-svg
body:
💡 **What**: Refactored independent sequential Prisma aggregate queries in `performanceController.js` to run concurrently using `Promise.all()`.
🎯 **Why**: The previous implementation performed multiple database roundtrips sequentially inside `.map()` loops, leading to N*M queries and a high overall latency.
📊 **Impact**: Reduces time complexity for these operations by a significant factor, potentially resulting in 3-5x faster responses for large numbers of consultants or months.
🔬 **Measurement**: Verified by observing the simulated time drop via a sequential vs concurrent benchmark script (261ms vs 52ms in 5-iteration simulation) and verified syntax checks.

author: kiryous
body:
Closes #46.

## Problem

`items 1 thru N of (messages of mailboxRef whose X)` throws AppleScript `-1728` on IMAP accounts (iCloud confirmed). Mail.app doesn't fully materialize remote message references, so the lazy list can't be sliced.

## Fix

Replace the slice with an in-loop counter:

```applescript
set matchedMessages to (messages of mailboxRef whose X)
set countSoFar to 0
repeat with msg in matchedMessages
  if maxCount > 0 and countSoFar >= maxCount then exit repeat
  …
  set countSoFar to countSoFar + 1
end repeat
```

`limit=0` (or unset) means no cap. Behavior for local mailboxes is unchanged since the `whose` filter still runs server-side.

## Test

Verified against an iCloud INBOX (~10k messages, 985 unread):

```python
search_messages(account="iCloud", sender_contains="apple.com", subject_contains="receipt", limit=10)
# → 10 results, no error
```

Existing unit tests still pass.

## Notes

- No API change.
- No new dependencies.

body:
Examina needed its repository-level requirements aligned with the PRD v2 definition: paper-first exam operations, role-driven workflows, end-to-end exam lifecycle, and analytics output expectations. This update codifies that spec in-repo so feature work can anchor to a single, explicit requirements source.

- **Requirements Baseline (PRD v2)**
  - Added a structured PRD section to `README.md` covering product overview, vision, user roles, and MVP constraints.
  - Captured the full exam lifecycle workflow (create → print → scan → process → grade → analytics).

- **Feature Scope Definition**
  - Documented functional expectations for:
    - Subject and student management
    - Exam and question creation
    - MCQ scantron + OMR flow
    - Theory script layout
    - Printing outputs
    - Scanning/grouping/correction
    - Grading and analytics/export

- **Product/UX/Architecture Guardrails**
  - Added UI principles (stepwise, low-clutter, hierarchy).
  - Added target stack references (React/Vite/TSX/Tailwind, Node backend, PostgreSQL, OCR/OMR/PDF toolchain).
  - Included future enhancement track for roadmap continuity.

- **Editorial consistency**
  - Standardized heading capitalization.
  - Clarified semicolon-separated subject input semantics, including subject names with spaces.

```md
- Subject management with semicolon-separated bulk input
  (for example: `English;Marketing;Further Mathematics`; spaces inside a subject name are allowed)
```

For local AI models, indicating that the service is free improves the UX compared to showing mathematically accurate but less reassuring zeroes.

Before: `$0.00`
After: `Free`

### ♿ Accessibility
Provides clear wording ('Free') that is natively understood by screen readers rather than forcing pronunciation of monetary zero values.

author: eriksherman
body:
Fixes #405

## Summary

- When images/PDFs are attached to an agent message, saves them to `{cwd}/.context/attachments/` on disk
- Appends file paths to the agent prompt so it can `Read`, copy, or move them in later turns
- Filenames use the original name when available, otherwise a content-hash (`attachment-{sha256}.png`)
- Non-fatal: if persistence fails, images still send inline as before

## Problem

Attachments are base64-encoded and sent inline to the agent. After that turn, they're gone — the agent literally says *"I don't have access to the screenshots you showed me in this conversation (they were viewed inline, not saved as files)."*

## Changes

- **New:** `packages/server/src/utils/context-attachments.ts` — `persistAttachments()` utility
- **Modified:** `packages/server/src/server/session.ts` — calls `persistAttachments()` in both `handleSendAgentMessageRequest` and the create-agent flow, passes file paths to `buildAgentPrompt()`

## How it works

1. User attaches `screenshot.png` to a message in workspace `~/myproject`
2. Server saves it to `~/myproject/.context/attachments/screenshot.png`
3. Agent receives the inline image AND a text block: `[Attached files saved to disk — you can read, copy, or move them: .context/attachments/screenshot.png]`
4. Agent can reference the file in any subsequent turn

## Test plan

- [ ] Attach an image to an agent message, verify `.context/attachments/` is created with the file
- [ ] Verify the agent can `Read` the persisted file in a follow-up turn
- [ ] Verify duplicate filenames get content-hashed names
- [ ] Verify failure to write (e.g. read-only fs) doesn't break message delivery

body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request and helping to improve Home Assistant. Please complete the following sections to help the processing and review of your changes. Please do not delete anything from this template. -->

## Summary
<!-- Provide a brief summary of the changes you have made and most importantly what they aim to achieve -->
Fixes three distinct crashes in the widget extension process that cause
widgets to go blank and not recover until the app is reinstalled.

- **ServerCache precondition crash** — `ServerCache.info.didSet` uses a
  `precondition` that reads `deletedServers` from shared UserDefaults on
  every check. When the main app deletes a server, the widget's cached
  `info` dict still contains it, causing the precondition to fail on the
  next mutation. Replaced with an error log, matching the existing pattern
  for the `server` dict. This was the most common crash (4 of 10 logs)
  and created a permanent crash loop only fixable by reinstalling.

- **Thread-unsafe `cachedApis` dictionary** — `AppEnvironment.cachedApis`
  is a plain dictionary accessed concurrently from multiple AppIntent
  threads (`ScriptAppIntent`, `SwitchIntent`), causing memory corruption.
  Added `NSLock` synchronization around all access.

- **`fatalError` in GRDB initialization** — When `DatabaseQueue` fails to
  open the on-disk database (locked file, corruption, file protection),
  the widget extension calls `fatalError`. Replaced with a fallback to an
  in-memory database, matching Realm's existing pattern.

author: williamzujkowski
body:
## Summary

Reopens the deferred kexec E2E test from closed PR #39. Third must-have of [v0.5.0 epic #40](https://github.com/williamzujkowski/aegis-boot/issues/40).

Root cause of PR #39's failure was busybox's \`mount -o loop\` silently "succeeding" with an empty mount point. Fix is in iso-parser, not the test: add a losetup fallback so discovery works regardless of whether the initramfs ships busybox or util-linux.

## Fix

\`OsIsoEnvironment::mount_iso\` now:
1. Tries \`mount -o loop,ro -t iso9660\` (works on util-linux).
2. Verifies the mount actually populated the mountpoint by reading a directory entry. Silent-fail from busybox → fall through.
3. Runs \`losetup -f --show -r <iso>\` to assign a loop device.
4. Runs \`mount -r -t iso9660 <loop> <mp>\`.
5. If that fails after losetup succeeded, detaches the loop device.

Works on both busybox (via fallback) and util-linux (fast path). No unsafe code added — pragmatic fix that keeps the crate boundary simple. A future rework could use \`mount(2)\` syscall directly from \`iso-parser\`, but that's a separate ADR.

## Test harness restoration

- \`scripts/qemu-kexec-e2e.sh\` — copies ISO from \`/dev/sr0\` to tmpfs file (mount flow needs a regular file, not a block-device symlink).
- \`.github/workflows/kexec-e2e.yml\` — installs util-linux in CI so losetup is definitely present; runs the test under \`sudo\` for loop-mount capability.

## Pass criteria

\`Linux version\` banner appears ≥ 2 times in serial (initial boot + post-kexec). Partial-pass fallback if kexec fires but serial is lost during the reboot (happens on some QEMU configs).

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test --workspace\` — 38 tests, all pass.
- [x] \`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings\` clean.
- [ ] CI: new \`kexec E2E\` job green.

body:
## Summary

- Add WebCodecs-based streaming video decode via mediabunny's forward `samples()` generator in a Web Worker
- Streaming is scoped to **transitions only** — regular playback uses DOM `<video>` elements (zero overhead, native audio/timing)
- Pre-warms both transition clips 3s before the transition starts, buffering decoded ImageBitmaps via a ring buffer
- Transition session renderer reads pre-decoded frames, falling through to DOM video on miss
- Position-aware decode throttle keeps the worker within 2.5s of playback, preventing buffer overflow
- Respects proxy toggle — streams use proxy URLs when enabled, restarts on toggle
- Debug: `window.__DEBUG__.setStreamingPlayback(true)` forces all-clip streaming

### Key files
- `streaming-decode-worker.ts` — Web Worker running mediabunny decode loop with throttle
- `streaming-playback.ts` — Main-thread coordinator: frame buffer, idle sweep, stream lifecycle
- `use-streaming-playback-controller.ts` — React hook: transition-scoped pre-warm, lookahead, proxy awareness
- `canvas-item-renderer.ts` — Streaming frame check before DOM video fallback
- `use-preview-transition-session-controller.ts` — Wires streaming provider into transition renderer

## Test plan

- [ ] Regular playback (no transition nearby) — no streaming overhead, DOM video handles everything
- [ ] Toggle proxy during playback — resolution switches without stuck frames
- [ ] Pause near transition, wait 3s, play — pre-warm buffers should be filled

author: nmgarza5
body:
## Description

Connectors currently die silently. When a connector fails repeatedly and enters the "repeated error" state, admins only discover it when they happen to check the connector list in the UI, or when a user complains about stale search results. There's no proactive notification.

This adds an in-app admin notification at the exact point where a connector transitions to repeated error state. The notification includes:
- Connector name and source type (e.g. "Google Drive", "Confluence")
- CC pair ID for linking to the connector's detail page

**How it works:**

The transition point is in `check_for_indexing` (runs every 15s). When `is_in_repeated_error_state()` detects consecutive failures and the connector wasn't already in that state, three things now happen:
1. `set_cc_pair_repeated_error_state(True)` — existing behavior
2. `create_notification()` — **new**: creates an admin notification with `user_id=None` (visible to all admins)
3. `task_logger.error()` — **new**: structured ERROR log for cloud monitoring

The notification uses `additional_data={"cc_pair_id": cc_pair.id}` for deduplication — if the same connector re-enters error state after recovery, a new notification is created. If it's already in error state and hasn't been dismissed, the timestamp is updated (existing `create_notification` behavior).

Uses the new `NotificationType.CONNECTOR_REPEATED_ERRORS` enum value.

**Linear:** [ENG-3983](https://linear.app/onyx-app/issue/ENG-3983/connector-invalid-admin-notification)

author: jtn0123
body:
## Summary

- `install/update.sh` `update_app_service()` used a 3-attempt loop with `sleep 1` between attempts, capping the service-startup wait at 3 seconds. On a Pi Zero 2 W the `inkypi` service routinely takes 5-8 seconds to become active (flask import + plugin discovery), so updates reported false failures while the service was fine moments later.
- Replaced the fixed-attempt loop with a `timeout 45` bounded wait and split the error message between a genuinely failed unit (`systemctl is-failed`) and a timeout, so the user knows whether to investigate or just be patient.
- The existing JTN-704 `EXIT` trap still captures the failure reason and clears the lockfile on either exit-1 branch; only the wait loop changed.

## Changes

- `install/update.sh`: replace 3x1s retry loop with `timeout 45 bash -c 'until systemctl is-active ...; do sleep 1; done'`, add `is-failed` branch + `systemctl status --no-pager` dump, keep existing `journalctl -n 20 --no-pager` tail.
- `tests/unit/test_install_scripts.py`: add `test_update_service_wait_uses_timeout_bound` — asserts `max_attempts` is gone, `timeout`+`45`+`is-failed` are present, timeout wording is distinct from failed state.

## Not touched

- Integration `tests/integration/test_update_failure_recovery.py`: the `INKYPI_UPDATE_TEST_*` hooks exit well before `update_app_service`, and exercising the new wait requires a real systemd. The regression is covered by the unit script-grep test instead, per the task guidance.

## Test plan

- [x] `SKIP_BROWSER=1 pytest tests/unit/test_install_scripts.py` — 207 passed
- [x] Full suite: 4180 passed, 4 skipped; 3 pre-existing CSS static failures confirmed present on `main` without this diff
- [x] `scripts/lint.sh` (ruff + black + shellcheck blocking) — clean

Closes JTN-706.

author: emmalouise2018
body:
## Summary

- Migration 395 included `-- +goose Up` / `-- +goose Down` blocks, but our custom migration runner executes the entire `.sql` file as a single query
- PostgreSQL treated the goose directives as comments and ran both the Up (widen to VARCHAR(500)) and Down (shrink back to VARCHAR(100)) blocks in the same transaction, effectively making the migration a no-op
- New migration 396 re-applies the same ALTER TABLE without goose syntax so the column widening actually persists

## Root Cause

The custom runner in `server/src/db/migrate.ts` does `client.query(migration.sql)` on the full file contents. Unlike goose, it doesn't parse `-- +goose Up` / `-- +goose Down` markers — they're just SQL comments. So both sections execute sequentially, and the Down block immediately reverts the Up block.

author: goevexx
body:
## Summary

Fixes slash commands being silently swallowed when a workflow is actively running. Previously, all messages during active execution were routed through the AI orchestrator, which saw the running workflow context and forwarded slash commands as workflow input rather than handling them as control commands.

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/orchestrator/orchestrator-agent.ts`** (+22 lines): Added a `parseCommand()` guard before active-workflow routing in `handleMessage`. Slash commands now always fall through to the existing deterministic command gate. Non-slash messages during active execution are blocked with an informative message referencing `/workflow cancel`.
- **`packages/core/src/orchestrator/orchestrator-agent.test.ts`** (+94 lines): Added `mockGetActiveWorkflowRun` to the `../db/workflows` mock module and a new `describe` block `'active workflow routing — slash command interception'` with 4 tests covering all routing paths.

## How It Works

**Before:** `handleMessage` → natural-language routing → AI orchestrator (slash commands swallowed)

**After:** `handleMessage` → `parseCommand()` first → if slash command: fall through to command handler; if not: check `getActiveWorkflowRun()` → block with guidance if running

The fix applies to all adapters (Telegram, Web UI, Slack, CLI, GitHub) since they all funnel through `handleMessage`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Type check (`bun x tsc --noEmit`) | ✅ Pass — no errors |
| Targeted tests (`bun test src/orchestrator/orchestrator-agent.test.ts`) | ✅ 96 passed, 0 failed |
| Full test suite (`bun run test`) | ✅ 337 passed, 3 pre-existing failures in `connection.test.ts` (unrelated — test-order env pollution, pass in isolation) |
| Build | ✅ No build needed — Bun runs TypeScript directly |

## Relation to PR #2

PR #2 fixed `/workflow cancel` for *paused* workflows by checking `getPausedWorkflowRun()` in command-handler.ts. This PR fixes the orthogonal case: ensuring *any* slash command reaches the command handler during *active* (running) execution, at the orchestrator routing layer.

Fixes #3

## Summary

- Covers the full lifecycle: agents → environments → sessions → streaming output
- Includes vault-based secret injection, GitHub repo mounting, and network configuration

## What this skill enables

- Create reusable agent definitions (model + system prompt + toolset)
- Provision cloud environments with custom packages and network policies
- Start sessions that mount GitHub repos and run the agent in an isolated container

This PR updates [virtualenv](https://pypi.org/project/virtualenv) from **20.24.2** to **21.2.4**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 21.2.4
   ```
   =================

- Security hardening: validate each entry of a seed wheel archive before extracting it so a tampered wheel cannot escape
  the app-data image directory via an absolute path or ``..`` traversal. (:issue:`3118`)
- Security hardening: verify the SHA-256 of every bundled seed wheel when it is loaded so a corrupted or tampered file
  on disk fails loud instead of being handed to pip. The hash table is generated alongside ``BUNDLE_SUPPORT`` by
  ``tasks/upgrade_wheels.py``. (:issue:`3119`)
- Security hardening: validate the distribution name and version specifier passed to ``pip download`` when acquiring a
  seed wheel so extras, pip flags, or shell metacharacters cannot be smuggled into the subprocess command line.
  (:issue:`3120`)
- Security hardening: replace the string-prefix containment check in ``virtualenv.util.zipapp`` with
  ``Path.relative_to`` so the zipapp extraction helpers refuse any path that does not resolve under the archive root.
  (:issue:`3121`)
- Security hardening: do not silently fall back to an unverified HTTPS context when the periodic update request to PyPI
  fails TLS verification. The returned metadata drives which wheel version virtualenv considers "up to date", so
  accepting an unverified response lets a network-level attacker suppress security updates. Set
  ``VIRTUALENV_PERIODIC_UPDATE_INSECURE=1`` to restore the previous behavior on hosts with broken trust stores.
  (:issue:`3122`)

No significant changes.
   ```

author: bboe
body:
## Summary

Replace the BCD `rtc_datetime` syscall with one that returns Unix epoch seconds, grow the C compiler just enough to consume it, and delete the BCD path. Three atomic commits:

- **`rtc_datetime` epoch syscall + `FUNCTION_PRINT_DATETIME`** — INT 30h / AH=30h now returns unsigned seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC in DX:AX, computed in the kernel with full-Gregorian leap math. A new shared `FUNCTION_PRINT_DATETIME` formats the value as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. `DIRECTORY_SECTOR` bumps to 15 to fit the larger stage 2.
- **`unsigned long` in cc.py + `date.c` migration** — adds the `unsigned long` type (only form accepted; bare `long` / `unsigned` are parse errors). Values live in DX:AX, locals occupy a 4-byte slot (or `dd 0` under main's elided frame). Scope is narrow: local declaration, init from `datetime()`, Var reference in a long context, store/load, and pass-by-value to a new `print_datetime` builtin. `datetime()` becomes zero-arg, `date.c` reduces to three lines, and the legacy path (SYS_RTC_DATETIME_LEGACY, FUNCTION_PRINT_BCD, shared_print_bcd, print_bcd builtin) is gone. SYS_RTC_UPTIME returns to 31h.
- **Peephole virtualization** — detects `unsigned long x = datetime(); print_datetime(x);` patterns where `x` is used exactly once and skips the memory round-trip. The compiled output matches the hand-written archive/date.asm byte-for-byte (15 bytes).

## Test plan
- [x] `./test_asm.py` — 21/21 pass at each of the three commits independently.
- [x] `date.c` compiles to the same 15 bytes as the archived hand-written version.
- [x] Manual smoke: bootable QEMU image builds via `./make_os.sh`.

# Description

First pass at adding first-class support on the context for compensation patterns to make exception handling, especially around child spawning, nicer and easier to reason about

Basic example:

```python
def saga_1() -> int:
    print("Performing operation 1")
    return 42

def saga_2() -> None:
    print("Performing operation 2")

    raise Exception("Something went wrong in operation 2")


@hatchet.task()
def simple(input: EmptyModel, ctx: Context) -> None:
    saga = ctx.begin_compensation_chain()

    s1 = saga.add(
        operation_fn=saga_1,
        compensation_fn=lambda: print("Compensating operation 1"),
    )

    print("s1:", s1)

    s2 = saga.add(
        operation_fn=saga_2,
        compensation_fn=lambda: print("Compensating operation 2"),
    )

    print("s2:", s2)
```

Which results in:

## Summary

- **Newsletter interest picker**: required radio group (Credit Cards / Software Development) on the subscribe form; selection is attached to the CTA event, **not** persisted to Listmonk.
- **Umami event consolidation**: every tracked click now uses a single Title Case event name with a structured `{ property }` payload so the dashboard stops sprawling and per-card/per-tab/per-category metrics become drilldowns instead of distinct event names.
- **Broken referral links**: refreshed URLs for Amex Business Platinum, Amex Delta Platinum Business, Chase Freedom Flex, and Chase Freedom Unlimited.
- **Card carousel reorder**: grouped by AMEX personal → Capital One personal → other personal → business.

## New event taxonomy

| Event name | Payload |
|---|---|
| `Subscribe Click` | `{ interest }` |
| `Credit Card Apply` | `{ card }` |
| `Tool Click` | `{ tool }` |
| `Smart Search` | `{ query }` (truncated to 100 chars) |
| `Nav Tab Click` | `{ tab }` |
| `Logo Click` | — |
| `Banner CTA Click` | `{ section }` |
| `Category Click` | `{ category }` |
| `Blog Card Click` | `{ post }` |
| `YouTube Video Click` | `{ video }` |
| `YouTube Channel Click` | — |
| `Consultation Click` | — |

Notable side effects of consolidation:
- `credit-card-apply-clicked` + `${cardName}-apply-clicked` → single `Credit Card Apply` event (also removes a `data-umami-event` that was double-counting per-card clicks via Umami's declarative handler).
- `smart-search-btn-click` + `${query}-SMART-SEARCH` → single `Smart Search` event (the old pattern created unbounded cardinality with one event name per unique query).
- Nav bar: 5 `* Tab Selected` events → one `Nav Tab Click` + `tab` property; desktop logo gets its own `Logo Click`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm run dev`, submit the newsletter form — verify Subscribe button gates on interest, Listmonk POST body is unchanged, and umami fires `Subscribe Click` with `{ interest }`.
- [ ] Click an Apply button on a credit card — verify exactly **one** umami request (`Credit Card Apply` + `{ card }`) and referral opens in a new tab.
- [ ] Click each nav tab + the desktop logo — verify `Nav Tab Click` with correct `tab` property, logo fires `Logo Click`.
- [ ] Click banner Programming/Credit Cards links, a category chip, a blog card, a YouTube card — verify drilldown payloads populate in Umami's Properties view.
- [ ] Verify refreshed referral links open the correct signup pages.
- [ ] Verify credit card carousel order matches the new grouping.

author: pnz1990
body:
## Summary

Closes #495. Replaces `ExecGitClient` (which shells out to the `git` binary) with `GoGitClient` using `github.com/go-git/go-git/v5`. All git operations now run in-process.

## Changes

### `pkg/scm/git_client.go`
- Removed: `ExecGitClient`, all `exec.Command("git", ...)` usage, `runGit*` helpers, `injectToken`
- Added: `GoGitClient` implementing the same `GitClient` interface
  - `Clone` → `gogit.PlainCloneContext` with `Depth:1, SingleBranch:true`
  - `Checkout` → `wt.Checkout`; creates branch if it doesn't exist
  - `CommitAll` → `wt.Add(".") + wt.Commit` with author/committer signature
  - `Push` → `repo.PushContext` with `BasicAuth{Username:"x-access-token", Password:token}`

### `cmd/kardinal-controller/main.go`
- `scm.NewExecGitClient()` → `scm.NewGoGitClient()`

### `Dockerfile`
- Stage 3 (runtime): removed `git` from `apk add`. Git binary is no longer required. Controller image is slightly smaller and has fewer CVE surface.

### `pkg/scm/scm_test.go`
- `TestInjectToken`: updated to use `NewGoGitClient`, guards with `testing.Short()` (go-git can hang on macOS automount paths)
- `TestGoGitClient_CheckoutCommitErrors`: new test verifying error propagation for Checkout/CommitAll on non-repo directories

## Note on macOS test skips
`go-git` `PlainInit`/`PlainOpen` can hang indefinitely on macOS when operating on temp dirs that traverse automount paths. This is a known macOS/NFS issue, not a go-git bug per se. Tests guard with `t.Skip` when `-short` is passed. CI runs on Ubuntu (linux/amd64) where go-git works correctly.

## Summary

- Adds blog post `src/content/blog/building-ai-toolkit-claude-code-plugins.md` (publishDate 2025-04-14, category `side-project`, tags: AI Tooling, Claude Code, Plugins, AWS) describing the aws-dev-toolkit Claude Code plugin with its 34 skills, 11 agents, and 3 MCP servers
- Adds work/project entry `src/content/work/aws-dev-toolkit.md` (title "AWS Dev Toolkit", startDate 2025-03-01) with matching description and tags

## Build & test results

- `npx astro check` — **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints** across all 26 Astro files
- `npx astro build` — **19 pages built successfully**, including `/work/aws-dev-toolkit/index.html` confirming the new project entry renders correctly

## Decisions

- Blog frontmatter follows existing conventions: `publishDate` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `img`/`img_alt` left empty (consistent with other posts that lack images), `description` as a block scalar
- Work frontmatter follows the Zod schema in `src/content/config.ts`: `startDate` as ISO 8601 (`2025-03-01T00:00:00Z`), `img` set to `/assets/aws-dev-toolkit.png` (required field per schema), `endDate` omitted to mark the project as ongoing
- No existing files were modified

## Agent notes

**What went well:** Astro's content collection system made validation straightforward — running `astro check` immediately catches frontmatter schema violations. The existing blog and work files provided clear templates to follow.

**What was difficult:** `mise run build` was not functional in the container environment (no tasks defined from the working directory), requiring a fallback to `npm install && npx astro check && npx astro build` directly.

**Patterns discovered:**
- Blog posts do not have a schema defined in `config.ts`; only the `work` collection is validated with Zod. Blog frontmatter conventions are inferred from existing files.
- The `work` collection requires `img` (non-optional string) — must always provide a value.
- Dates in `work` entries use full ISO 8601 format; blog `publishDate` uses plain `YYYY-MM-DD`.

**Suggestions for future tasks:**
- Consider defining a Zod schema for the blog collection in `config.ts` to get the same validation guarantees as `work`
- A placeholder image asset at `/public/assets/aws-dev-toolkit.png` would complete the project entry visually

### Motivation
- Decomposing a world→body Z-up quaternion with ZYX Euler can produce an apparent yaw for pure-tilt orientations due to rotation-order coupling, which corrupts error statistics.
- The wave generator already writes explicit Euler fields (`roll_deg`, `pitch_deg`, `yaw_deg`) that represent the intended reference attitude without that artifact.
- We should prefer the explicit CSV Euler values when present while keeping a safe fallback for legacy/malformed rows.

### Description
- Added a helper `reference_euler_from_csv(...)` in `src/util/W3dSimCommon.cpp` that prefers `imu.roll_deg/pitch_deg/yaw_deg` when finite and falls back to `quat_wb_zu_to_euler_nautical(...)` otherwise.
- Replaced the prior direct per-record reference assignment in `W3dSimulationRunner::run` with a call to the new helper, ensuring consistent behavior for each sample.
- Change is localized to `src/util/W3dSimCommon.cpp` and preserves existing mag/noise handling and output format.

body:
## Summary

Python Lint has been failing on every open PR (including #105) because of 58 pre-existing ruff errors in files the PRs didn't touch. This PR clears the backlog so the lint gate can go green again.

Run before: `Found 58 errors.`
Run after:  `All checks passed!`

## Error breakdown

| Code | Count | What it is |
|------|-------|------------|
| F401 | 43 | Unused imports |
| E402 | 14 | Module-level imports after non-import code |
| F841 | 3  | Unused local variable assignments |
| F541 | 1  | f-string with no placeholders (`backtester.py:81`) |

Source (`the_similarity/`):
- `api.py` — 5 unused imports (`normalize`, `ProgressEvent`, `MonteCarloResult`, `RegimeConditionalResult`, `ConformalResult`). `ProgressEvent` is still exported to consumers via `the_similarity/__init__.py` which imports it from `core.matcher` directly.

- `core/backtester.py` — unused `dataclasses.field`; stray `f""` with no placeholders

- `core/feature_store.py` — unused `typing.Any`
- `core/matcher.py` — **13 E402s**: hoisted late module-level imports to the top. Investigated first; there's no circular-import reason for the split, just a `ProgressEvent` dataclass and `ProgressCallback` alias that had been wedged between the `Config` import and the rest. Moved imports up, kept the type declarations below.
- `core/projector.py` — unused `dataclasses.field`
- `core/strategy.py` — unused `regime.tag_regime`
- `methods/dtw_matcher.py` — unused `core.normalizer.normalize`

Tests (`the_similarity/tests/`):
- `test_alerts.py`, `test_auth.py`, `test_embedding.py`, `test_emd.py`, `test_ensemble.py`, `test_koopman.py`, `test_portfolio.py`, `test_regime.py`, `test_strategy.py`, `test_terrain.py`, `test_wavelet_leaders.py` — F401 unused imports. Each one verified not used via fixtures, `pytest.raises`/`mark`/`approx`.

body:
## Summary

Adds a graphify skill to the agent template, enabling any cortextos agent to navigate a codebase using a pre-built AST knowledge graph instead of reading raw source files.

## Why

Reading source files to answer structural questions is expensive: understanding how FastChecker connects to AgentManager might require reading 5+ files (~10,000 tokens). The same query against a graphify knowledge graph costs ~400 tokens — a 25x reduction.

## What

`templates/agent/.claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md` covers:
- **Setup**: `pip install graphifyy && graphify update <project>` (zero LLM tokens, pure AST)
- **Git hooks**: `graphify hook install` — auto-rebuilds graph on every commit and checkout
- **Obsidian wiring**: copy `graph.json` + `GRAPH_REPORT.md` to vault for persistent access
- **Commands**: `query`, `explain`, `path` with `--budget` flag
- **Benchmark**: `graphify benchmark` to measure reduction on your codebase
- **When to use / when not to use**: guidance so agents don't over-apply it

## Benchmarks (cortextos codebase)

| Query type | Reduction |
|-----------|-----------|
| Structural ("what is the main entry point") | 466x |
| Behavioral ("how does X work") | 34x |
| Average across all queries | 22x |

Graph: 1,377 nodes, 2,570 edges, 195 communities — built from 350 files in seconds, zero LLM cost.

## Test plan
- [ ] Skill file present at correct path
- [ ] Trigger keywords cover "how does X work", "graphify", "code graph"
- [ ] No deployment-specific paths hardcoded (uses `<project-root>` placeholder)

## Summary

Implements **E9-B02: Collector Agent** — the first stage of the multi-agent research pipeline from Epic 9.

- Adds `packages/compiler/src/agents/collector.ts` exporting `collectEvidence(db, workspacePath, taskId, options?)`.
- Reads the task's `brief.md`, builds a stop-word-filtered **OR-joined** FTS5 query (wide-net recall, BM25 still ranks), searches compiled wiki via kernel `searchPages`.
- Writes each matched page to `tasks/tsk-<id>/evidence/NN-<slug>.md` with YAML frontmatter citing `source_path`, `source_title`, `source_type`, `rank`, `collected_at`, `truncated`.
- Emits `evidence.collect` trace per file and transitions the task from `created` → `collecting` (which emits a `task.transition` trace).
- Bodies longer than `maxExcerptChars` (default 4000) are truncated with a `[...truncated]` marker so downstream summarizer input stays bounded.
- Pure deterministic module — no Claude API calls. Operates entirely over the kernel's search/tasks/traces surface.

## Error handling

Never throws. Returns `err(Error)` for: task missing, task not in `created`, `brief.md` missing, brief body empty, no searchable terms after stop-word filter, zero wiki matches (task stays in `created` so the operator can refine the brief or add sources), filesystem errors.

- [x] 16 integration tests with real workspace + real FTS5 index + real task records
  - [x] Happy path: evidence files created, frontmatter cites source, state transitions to `collecting`, rank-ordered `NN-` filename prefixes, trace events emitted

  - [x] Error paths (6): missing task, wrong status, missing `brief.md`, empty brief body, unsearchable brief (all stop words), zero matches
  - [x] Idempotency: second call on same task rejected
- [x] Full suite: **907 tests pass** (types 13 + kernel 240 + compiler 348 + cli 306)
- [x] `pnpm lint` clean, `pnpm typecheck` clean

author: ygabrielmachado
body:
Root cause: SNS topics encrypted with alias/aws/sns block CloudWatch Alarms
from publishing, the AWS-managed key policy does not grant access to
cloudwatch.amazonaws.com. Discovered during sandbox validation when alarms
transitioned to ALARM correctly but no emails were ever delivered.

Module fixes:
- modules/monitoring/cloudwatch-alarms: create dedicated customer-managed
  KMS key with explicit grants to sns.amazonaws.com and cloudwatch.amazonaws.com;
  remove default_value from metric_transformation (was producing zero-flooded
  metrics); set evaluation_periods=2, datapoints_to_alarm=1, treat_missing_data
  =ignore to tolerate CloudTrail → CloudWatch Logs ingestion lag; add
  invokedBy NOT EXISTS and eventType != AwsServiceEvent to unauthorized_api_calls
  filter to exclude false positives from AWS service-linked roles
- modules/monitoring/guardduty, electronic-signatures/mfa-enforcement,
  access-control/session-policies: remove kms_master_key_id from SNS topics
  (payload is alert metadata, not PHI)
- modules/audit-trail/dynamodb-audit/lambda/audit_processor.py: append
  sequence_number to timestamp range key to prevent collisions when
  multiple stream events share the same second (preserved event_timestamp
  field for human-readable ISO 8601)
- modules/audit-trail/dynamodb-audit, modules/data-integrity/immutable-storage,
  modules/audit-trail/cloudtrail, modules/electronic-signatures/signature-logging:
  add object_lock_mode (COMPLIANCE/GOVERNANCE) and enable_deletion_protection
  variables to support sandbox teardown; defaults remain production-compliant
- modules/*: replace parentheses/commas in CFRSection tag values with
  hyphens/slashes to comply with AWS tag value regex

Sandbox tooling:
- examples/sandbox: self-contained plug-and-play deployment with 1-day
  retention, GOVERNANCE mode, and deletion protection off; TF_VAR_sandbox_email
  override for real notifications
- scripts/sandbox.sh: wrapper providing plan/apply/destroy commands; destroy
  empties Object Lock buckets using --bypass-governance-retention before
  terraform destroy

Validation improvements:
- scripts/validate-audit-trail.sh: add --enable-sns-test flag that triggers
  GuardDuty sample findings + 10 cross-account AssumeRole attempts to
  exercise the full alarm → SNS → email pipeline

Documentation:
- docs/architecture-decisions.md: add ADR-013 documenting the KMS/SNS issue,
  the customer-managed key pattern, and the generalized lesson for future
  cross-service AWS integrations
- docs/validation-guide.md: add troubleshooting section with 8 failure modes
  (symptom, root cause, diagnostic command, resolution) — serves as OQ
  evidence for operational issues and their resolution
- docs/faq.md: add FAQ entries for "alarm in ALARM but no email",
  "alarm firing on service-linked roles", and "destroying sandbox with
  Object Lock"
- examples/sandbox/README.md: document TF_VAR_sandbox_email, --enable-sns-test
  workflow, and link to troubleshooting guide
- scripts/sandbox.sh: help text now includes env vars and workflow examples

author: jaywhy13
body:
The Django URL config only mapped the root path ('') to the React
index.html. Any React Router path navigated to directly — such as
/meal-plan/3 shared via a link — hit Django's custom_404 handler and
returned a JSON 404 response instead of loading the app.

Added a re_path catch-all at the bottom of urlpatterns that serves
index.html for any path not matched by a prior rule. Placing it last
ensures it does not shadow the API (/api/), admin (/admin/), or health
check routes.

The custom_404 handler is now only reachable for programmatic 404s
raised explicitly within views via raise Http404, which is the correct
behaviour for an API — browser navigation is handled by React Router.

author: thaynes43
body:
## Summary

- Introduces a `flux-local` GitHub Actions workflow that validates HelmRelease + Kustomization rendering on every PR touching `kubernetes/**`, for **both** the `main` and `edge` cluster roots.
- Posts a sticky PR comment per `(cluster, resource)` showing the rendered diff, so reviewers see what will *actually* hit the API server (not just the YAML diff).
- Adds `docs/renovate/README.md` — the staged auto-merge roadmap (Tiers 0–4) drawing from `onedr0p/home-ops` and `bjw-s-labs/home-ops`.
- Sets up the precondition for every later tier: nothing should auto-merge without a real validation gate, and right now there isn't one.

## Why this first

Today there is no PR-gating CI. Any `automerge: true` rule (we already have one for github-actions) is flying blind. `flux-local test` actually renders every chart at the pinned version with our values, so it catches:

- Chart upgrades whose values schema changed and our `values:` block no longer validates
- Variable substitution failures
- Missing or invalid CRDs
- Anything that would only fail at `flux reconcile` time

Once this lands and is required on `main`, the rest of the renovate roadmap (trusted-package auto-merge, HA grouping, etc.) becomes safe to roll out.

## What's in the workflow

- **`filter`** — `bjw-s-labs/action-changed-files` skips the workflow when no `kubernetes/**` files changed.
- **`test`** — matrix over `[main, edge]`, runs `flux-local test --enable-helm --all-namespaces` against `kubernetes/{cluster}/flux`. Edge stays in the matrix even while powered off — this only validates YAML, no cluster contact.
- **`diff`** — matrix over `[main, edge] x [helmrelease, kustomization]` (4 jobs). Checks out both PR branch and `main`, runs `flux-local diff` between them, posts a sticky comment via `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` keyed on `pr#/cluster/resource`.
- **`success`** — depends on `test` + `diff`, aggregates pass/fail/skip into one job. **This is the job to add to branch protection** — not `test`/`diff` directly, since they have skip conditions and "skipped" looks like "missing" to required-checks.

Uses default `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Switching to a GitHub App (so auto-merged commits trigger downstream workflows) is documented in the roadmap as a follow-up.

## Things to verify before requiring this check

1. **First green run.** This PR itself should produce a green `Flux Local - Success` check. If `flux-local test` fails, it's almost certainly one of:
   - SOPS-encrypted secret rendering (`kubernetes/main/flux/vars/cluster-secrets.sops.yaml`). May need `--skip-secrets` or a `flux-local` config file. Watch the test job logs.
   - Edge cluster path — confirm `kubernetes/edge/flux` is structurally compatible with `flux-local` even while the cluster is off.
2. **Diff comment quality.** Open the rendered diff comment on this PR (it'll be empty since we didn't touch `kubernetes/**`, so trigger it by manually pushing a tiny no-op chart bump to a branch later if needed). Check that `--strip-attrs` is filtering enough noise.
3. **Workflow runtime.** Should be ~2–4 min. If much longer, look at whether `--enable-helm` is fetching charts that could be cached.

## After this merges

1. Add `Flux Local - Success` as a required status check in branch protection for `main`.
2. Open the **Phase 1.5 PR**: split `.github/renovate.json5` into `.renovate/*.json5` files (mirror onedr0p/bjw-s layout). Has to be a separate PR because Renovate's `extends` resolves from the default branch, so the files have to exist on `main` before the root config can extend them.
3. Open the **Tier 2 PR**: trusted-package auto-merge rules (own `ghcr.io/thaynes43/*` digests, `kube-prometheus-stack` minor/patch), with `ignoreTests: false` so this gate actually gates them.

## Test plan

- [ ] `Flux Local - Filter` runs and produces a non-empty `changed-files` (this PR doesn't touch `kubernetes/**`, so it'll be empty — that's expected; verify the skip path works).
- [ ] `Flux Local - Success` job goes green via the skip path on this PR.
- [ ] After merge, manually trigger the workflow against a throwaway branch that bumps a chart version, confirm `test` runs and `diff` posts a comment.
- [ ] Add `Flux Local - Success` to branch protection on `main`.

body:
Builds the Shipping Ship Ships web app from Book 3 of the NSS curriculum — three interactive lists (Docks, Hauling Ships, Shipping Ships) wired with click events that surface relationship data via browser alerts.

## Data model
```
DOCK (1) ──< HAULER (1) ──< SHIPPINGSHIP
```
Each shipping ship has a `haulerId` FK; each hauler has a `dockId` FK.

## Modules
- **`scripts/database.js`** — single source of truth; exports `getDocks`, `getHaulingShips`, `getShippingShips` (each returns a shallow copy)
- **`scripts/DockList.js`** — renders docks; click shows all haulers currently unloading at that dock (or "nothing")
- **`scripts/HaulerList.js`** — renders haulers with `data-id`/`data-type`; click counts how many shipping ships are assigned to it
- **`scripts/ShippingShipList.js`** — renders ships with `data-hauler-id`; click resolves and names the hauler carrying it
- **`scripts/main.js`** — composes all three lists into `#container`

## Click interaction example
```js
// ShippingShipList click handler
if (itemClicked.dataset.type === "shippingShip") {
    const haulerId = parseInt(itemClicked.dataset.haulerId)
    const haulingShip = getHaulingShips().find(h => h.id === haulerId) ?? { name: "Incorrect" }
    window.alert(`${itemClicked.textContent.trim()} is being hauled by ${haulingShip.name}`)
}
```

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Determine if the user (GeorgeST1302) can fully replicate the functionality of stanfordnlp/dspy in their own repository (price-tracker) on the master branch, including installation, usage, and any limitations based on common student hardware (e.g., no paid API access, typical laptop specs). If not fully replicable, outline the possible limitations and provide guidance for maximum achievable replication with free/local resources.

The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: LIKE ALWAYS WHAT DOES THIS PAPER WHAT PROBEO DOS IT OSLVE  ,WHERE IS NEUROSYMBOLIC AI USED DOI I NEEED API IF NO OKAY EXPLAIN ME IN SIMPLE HUGE SENETCENS SO I UNDESRSTAND AN EXPLAIN TEAHFER 

Assistant: The “paper” you’re referring to is almost certainly **DSPy** (the framework from the repo `stanfordnlp/dspy`). It’s trying to solve this problem:

## What problem does it solve?
When people build LLM apps, they often do something like:  
- write a prompt by hand,  
- try it,  
- tweak words,  
- try again,  
- repeat forever.

That approach is **fragile** (small changes break it), **hard to scale** (lots of prompts), and **hard to improve systematically** (no clear way to “train” prompts like you train ML models).

**DSPy’s goal** is to let you build LLM systems more like *real machine learning pipelines*:  
- you describe what the system should do using **modules** (like “classify”, “extract”, “answer with citations”, etc.),  
- you provide **a metric** (what “good” means) and **some examples**,  
- and then DSPy can **automatically optimize the prompts / instructions / few-shot examples** (and sometimes other settings) so the system performs better on your metric.

So in very simple terms:  
**DSPy tries to replace “prompt guessing” with “prompt optimization.”**

## What does it “probe” / “prove”?
If by “probe/prove” you mean what the work is demonstrating, it’s basically showing:

- You can treat prompting as something you can **compile/optimize**, not just hand-write.
- With a small dataset and a scoring rule, you can often get **better accuracy** than manual prompting.
- Multi-step LLM pipelines (like retrieve → reason → answer) can be made more reliable if they’re optimized as a system.

## Where is NeuroSymbolic AI used here?
**Neuro-symbolic AI** usually means:  
- *neural parts* (LLMs, embeddings, learned models)  
combined with  
- *symbolic parts* (structured rules, typed signatures, constraints, program-like composition, search/optimization).

In DSPy, the “symbolic/program” side is things like:
- you write a **structured program** of steps/modules (“first retrieve, then generate, then verify…”),
- each module has a **signature** (inputs/outputs) and a clear role,
- and the system can do **search/optimization** over prompt components.

The “neural” side is the LLM itself (and optionally retrievers / embedding models).

So neuro-symbolic is used in DSPy because it’s basically:  
**LLM intelligence + structured program architecture + automatic optimization/search**.

## Do you need an API?
Usually, **yes, you need access to an LLM somehow**, because DSPy is not the LLM; it is a framework that *calls* an LLM.

But you do **not** necessarily need a *paid* cloud API.

You have options:

1) **Cloud API** (OpenAI / Anthropic / etc.)  
- easiest setup  
- costs money per token

2) **Local model** (running on your machine)  
- no paid API required  
- you still need software + enough compute (GPU helps a lot)

3) **Hosted open-source providers** (sometimes free tiers)  
- still technically an API, but not necessarily OpenAI

If you tell me your situation (PC specs, do you have a GPU, do you want totally free), I can tell you the most realistic path.

## Where is this useful in real life?
DSPy / neuro-symbolic style LLM programming is useful when you need:

- **Question answering with retrieval (RAG)** for a company docs / PDFs
- **Information extraction** (turn emails, notes, medical text, contracts into structured fields)
- **Chatbots that must follow rules** (format, constraints, required fields)
- **Multi-step workflows** (plan → call tools → verify → final answer)
- **Systems you want to improve with evaluation** rather than just “vibes”

## One simple “teacher explanation” sentence
“DSPy is a way to build LLM applications like a machine-learning system: instead of hand-writing prompts and guessing, you write a structured pipeline and let the system automatically optimize the prompts using examples and a scoring rule so the results get better and more reliable.”

This change connects the 2.5D LBM macro wind simulation to the decor rendering system. 

Key changes:
1. **LBM Simulation**: Resized the simulation grid to 64x60 to ensure the resulting WindDataUbo stays within the guaranteed 64KB limit for OpenGL uniform buffers.

author: superninja-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

After PR #283 fixed the novelty classification, the 2026-(W) PCGS MS70 Silver Eagle is now correctly identified as `coins_bullion` — but **the year reads as '2020' instead of '2026'**. Gemini's vision model consistently misreads the digit '6' as '0' on PCGS slab labels.

## Root Cause

The digit '6' on machine-printed PCGS labels looks similar to '0' to Gemini's vision. Previous warnings only mentioned '2021' as a misread — but '2020' is the most common actual error.

## Changes

### 1. Detail Extractor — Slab Label Year Reading (`detailExtractor.ts`)
- **New section** in coin extraction prompt: `YEAR IDENTIFICATION (CRITICAL FOR SLABBED COINS)`
  - Read year from SLAB LABEL, not coin face
  - Explicit warning: '2026' is frequently misread as '2020', '2021', '2024', '2006'
  - Digit shape hints: '6 has a tail curving DOWN-LEFT, 0 has a round shape'
  - Cross-check: if itemName year differs from slab label, trust the label

### 2. Year Override — Title + Description Fix (`detailExtractor.ts`)
- Previously only corrected `specs["Year"]` (item specifics)
- **Now also corrects the eBay title and description** when a year mismatch is detected
- Preserves mint mark suffixes (e.g., '2020-(W)' → '2026-(W)')
- Replaces all occurrences of wrong year in description

### 3. Expanded Misread Warnings (`index.ts` + `domainPrompts.ts`)
- Pass 1 prompt: Added '2020' to known misread list, added digit shape hints
- Domain prompt: Same updates to SLAB LABEL IS TRUTH rule

## Expected Result
Even if Pass 1 and Pass 2 misread '2026' as '2020', the detail extractor (separate focused vision pass) should catch the correct year from the slab label and override the title/description/specs.

author: izabael
body:
## Summary

Redirects /for-agents from a 545-line developer documentation page into a **cube-centric 200-line page** whose entire job is to hand the visitor a Playground Cube they can copy-paste into any AI chat. Everything that used to be on /for-agents moves to the new **/for-agents/advanced** page for developers who want the API reference.

Stacked on \`izabael/lexicon-phase1\` because it touches the same /for-agents surface iza-3 just finished editing.

### The problem this solves

From Marlowe's message tonight:
> *"I want something any reasonably modern LLM can just read and know what to do. You can have an ADVANCED page for all the more complex shit."*

The old /for-agents assumed a terminal and walked the reader through curl + Python + JSON. But for ChatGPT Free / Claude Free / Gemini Free users without tool access, the curl instruction is read-only. They can see it; they can't execute it. And for mobile users, copy-paste between browser and native chat app is 5+ taps of friction.

The cube was already designed to be the paste-in payload. The /for-agents page should just hand one out.

### What changed

1. **\`content/cubes/playground.txt\`** — swapped the descriptive "WHAT TO DO" face for an action-oriented **"OFFER YOUR HUMAN"** face that acts as the LLM's cheat sheet: _Play The Chamber / Read #lobby / Meet Zeus or Selene / Pick a persona from /workshop / Register an agent_. The LLM reading the cube stops summarizing the site and starts offering the user concrete choices. Also added a no-terminal fallback to HOW TO JOIN: _"If you cannot POST, send them to /join (30-second form, no terminal needed)."_ Full face alignment preserved at 97 cols (verified).

2. **\`frontend/templates/for-agents.html\`** — complete rewrite. 200 lines instead of 545. Mission banner + hero ("Copy this cube. Paste it into any AI chat. Your AI will know what to do.") + rendered Playground cube inside a themed \`<pre>\` block + two buttons:
   - **📋 Copy cube** (all browsers, \`navigator.clipboard.writeText\` with textarea fallback)
   - **🦋 Share to your AI** (mobile only, auto-detected via \`navigator.share\`, opens the native share sheet with Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini/Grok/Messages all listed)

   Theme-aware: inherits all seven themes via base.html. **Phosphor + cube = 1984 terminal aesthetic** as an emergent feature.

3. **\`frontend/templates/for-agents-advanced.html\`** — new template, holds everything that used to be on /for-agents: API reference, endpoints table, register-in-one-call curl + Python examples, persona templates, agent card format, rules, required/optional fields, leave-a-message form. Dev-dialect reference for humans who want to read docs. Back-link at top.

4. **\`app.py\`** — \`_for_agents_render()\` now loads \`playground.txt\` via \`_load_cube("playground")\` and passes \`playground_cube_text\` into the ctx dict. New \`/for-agents/advanced\` route registered BEFORE the \`/{shortcut}\` catchall so "advanced" routes correctly instead of falling into the personalization shim.

### The mobile handshake that now works

1. User lands on /for-agents from any chat app
2. Taps "Share to your AI"
3. Native iOS/Android share sheet opens with **every installed AI app** listed
4. Picks one — cube text lands pre-formatted in the target app's input
5. Hits send, AI reads the cube, AI responds by offering specific next actions from the OFFER YOUR HUMAN face

Zero terminal. Zero curl assumption. The tool-use gap between Claude Pro and ChatGPT Free stops mattering because the cube content IS the context the LLM needs — no tool required to respond helpfully.

## Test plan

- [ ] /for-agents renders with the cube visible, mission banner, copy button, (mobile) share button
- [ ] Copy button writes cube text to clipboard with toast confirmation
- [ ] On desktop, Share button is hidden (navigator.share undefined)
- [ ] On mobile, Share button is visible and opens the share sheet
- [ ] /for-agents/advanced renders the full reference with back-link to /for-agents
- [ ] /for-agents/sdk and other shortcuts still work (catchall intact)
- [ ] Cube OFFER YOUR HUMAN face reads correctly — LLM pasting the cube should offer the 5 options
- [ ] Cube face alignment — 97 cols, all 14 lines match (verified)
- [ ] All 7 themes render the page correctly (Netzach + Phosphor especially)
- [ ] The page works as JSON (Accept: application/json) — falls back to FOR_AGENTS_DATA as before

author: anmolg1997
body:
## Summary

Adds `DatabaseMemoryService`, a durable, SQL-backed memory service that works with any SQLAlchemy-compatible async database (SQLite via `aiosqlite`, PostgreSQL via `asyncpg`, MySQL/MariaDB, etc.).

- Fills the gap between the volatile `InMemoryMemoryService` and the cloud-only Firestore/Vertex AI options. Gives self-hosted deployments a persistent memory backend with **zero cloud dependencies**
- Mirrors the keyword-extraction approach of `FirestoreMemoryService` and reuses the SQLAlchemy patterns from `DatabaseSessionService`
- Implements `add_session_to_memory`, `add_events_to_memory` (delta ingestion), and `search_memory`
- Includes lazy table creation with double-checked locking, async context manager support, and proper rollback-on-exception handling

## Motivation

Currently, developers not using Vertex AI or Google Cloud Firestore have no persistent memory option. `InMemoryMemoryService` is explicitly volatile and loses all data on restart. This is a frequently requested feature:

- Closes #2524, "Add support for additional Memory Bank services: DatabaseMemoryService"
- Closes #2976, "SQLite-based memory service implementation"

## Design Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Placed in `google.adk.memory` (not `integrations/`) | Follows `DatabaseSessionService` placement in `sessions/`, and uses no external cloud SDK |
| Reuses `DynamicJSON` from `sessions.schemas.shared` | Consistent JSON/JSONB handling across SQLAlchemy services |
| Separate `_memory_schemas.py` for ORM models | Mirrors the `sessions/schemas/` pattern, keeps concerns separated |
| Keyword search (not semantic/vector) | Matches FirestoreMemoryService approach. Semantic search can be added via a future `SearchBackend` abstraction |
| Lazy `__getattr__` import in `__init__.py` | Matches `DatabaseSessionService` pattern, avoids hard SQLAlchemy dependency for users who don't need it |

## Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `src/google/adk/memory/database_memory_service.py` | New: `DatabaseMemoryService` implementation |
| `src/google/adk/memory/_memory_schemas.py` | New: SQLAlchemy ORM model (`StorageMemoryEntry`) |
| `src/google/adk/memory/__init__.py` | Updated: lazy export of `DatabaseMemoryService` |
| `tests/unittests/memory/test_database_memory_service.py` | New: 19 tests covering CRUD, search, scoping, dedup, persistence |

## Usage

```python
from google.adk.memory import DatabaseMemoryService

# SQLite (zero-config)
memory = DatabaseMemoryService("sqlite+aiosqlite:///memory.db")

# PostgreSQL
memory = DatabaseMemoryService("postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@host/db")

async with memory:
    await memory.add_session_to_memory(session)
    result = await memory.search_memory(
        app_name="my_app", user_id="u1", query="agent tool usage"
    )
```

## Test plan

- [x] 19 unit tests passing (`pytest tests/unittests/memory/test_database_memory_service.py`)
- [x] All 59 existing memory tests still pass (`pytest tests/unittests/memory/`)
- [x] Code formatted with `isort` + `pyink` per CONTRIBUTING.md
- [x] Tested with in-memory SQLite and file-based SQLite
- [x] Context manager lifecycle (`__aenter__`/`__aexit__`) verified

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Goal

Redesign `/control` into an immersive, fullscreen-feeling driving HUD inspired by rally / racing game UX (closer to WRC-style game presentation), while keeping the real RC driving constraints and existing race/duel/chat systems. This PR is **PR 1 of a staged roadmap** and should implement the **foundation/layout architecture only** — not the full visual polish of every later feature.

The user explicitly wants a complete blueprint and a PR-by-PR rollout. Start with the structural foundation so later PRs can layer on telemetry, race/duel widgets, and debug tools cleanly.

---

## Product direction

`/control` should stop being a traditional webpage with stacked panels and become:

- a **camera-first fullscreen control surface**
- with **overlay HUD layers**
- and **hidden/drawer-based secondary UI**
- with **debug mode** available for operators/testers

No permanent mouse-driving buttons in the main player experience. They may remain available only in debug mode or hidden fallback mode.

The long-term target experience is:
- player sees mostly the camera feed
- small immersive HUD overlays show only essential info
- duel/race/chat are compact and non-blocking
- extra systems live in left/right drawers

---

## User-confirmed UX requirements

### Always-visible info (player HUD)
Keep visible in the immersive HUD:
- Battery
- Speed
- Ping
- Session timer (very subtle / non-anxious presentation)
- Race/duel status only when active
- Temporary input visualization while testing without hardware (so control commands can be verified)

### Drawers
- **Left drawer**: races / duels / leaderboard context
- **Right drawer**: chat

### Visual style
- Closer to a **racing game HUD** (WRC-style inspiration)
- Big, clear speed emphasis
- Minimalist, low visual noise
- Fullscreen-feeling without forcing browser fullscreen API

### Debug mode
Need a proper debug/operator mode, because testing without hardware is important.
This should allow keeping tools like:
- command log
- optional mouse driving fallback controls
- extra telemetry / diagnostics
without polluting the standard player UI.

### During race / duel
Need support (later PRs can refine the visuals) for showing:
- opponent name
- checkpoints
- duel ratings (self + opponent) when in duel

---

# THIS PR (PR 1) SCOPE

Implement the new **layout foundation** and **UI architecture** for `/control`.
This PR should establish the structure that later PRs can build on.

## Deliverables in this PR

### 1. Rebuild `frontend/control.html` into overlay-based layout
Replace the old stacked page composition with a structure like this (exact naming may vary if clearer, but keep it clean and future-proof):

- root control shell
- fullscreen camera stage
- HUD overlay root
- top HUD strip
- bottom HUD strip / speed area
- center overlay root (for countdowns / transient alerts)
- left drawer (race / duel / leaderboard)
- right drawer (chat)
- debug panel container (hidden by default unless debug mode enabled)

Keep existing systems wired in, but re-home them into the new structure.

The page should feel fullscreen and immersive immediately on load, even without browser fullscreen API.

### 2. Preserve existing functionality while relocating it
Do not break:
- session lifecycle
- camera feed
- race panel features
- duel panel features
- chat drawer functionality
- summary overlay
- session warnings
- countdowns

These can be moved into drawers / overlay containers / compact regions, but they must remain functional.

### 3. Introduce player mode vs debug mode structure
Add a lightweight debug mode mechanism.

Requirements:
- default = immersive player mode
- debug mode activated by query param `?debug=1`
- in debug mode, show additional operator/testing UI containers
- existing big mouse control buttons may be kept only in debug mode (or a debug-only fallback section)
- command log should be debug-only

The user explicitly wants temporary input visualization while testing without hardware, but this should not pollute the permanent player experience.

### 4. Add immersive HUD placeholders / containers
Create clean HUD slots for:
- battery
- speed (prominent)
- ping
- session timer (small/subtle)
- active mode/race/duel status
- temporary input visualization area for non-hardware testing

This PR does **not** need to perfect the final artwork, but the structure and basic styling should clearly move toward a game-HUD feel.

### 5. Add left/right drawer system suitable for later extensions
Implement drawer shells with show/hide hooks and buttons/hotspots.

- left drawer: race/duel context
- right drawer: chat
- should not dominate the page by default
- should be non-destructive overlays, not layout-breaking sidebars
- should work in immersive mode

### 6. Create CSS foundation for immersive racing HUD style
Update `frontend/styles/control.css` heavily as needed.

- camera fills viewport

- large speed emph...

body:
Implements the `@apic-vibe-portal/shared` TypeScript package — the canonical type definitions for the frontend-BFF API contract.

### Package setup
- Dual CJS/ESM build via separate `tsconfig.esm.json` and `tsconfig.cjs.json` with `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` for TS 6.0
- CJS output gets a nested `{"type":"commonjs"}` `package.json` to resolve correctly under the parent `"type":"module"` package
- `exports` field in `package.json` maps `import`/`require` conditions to the correct output
- Portable Node.js-based build/clean scripts (no shell-specific commands); `jest` invoked via PATH with `NODE_OPTIONS`

### Domain types
- **Enums**: `ApiLifecycle`, `ApiKind`, `GovernanceStatus`, `EnvironmentKind` — string enums for runtime usability
- **Models**: `ApiDefinition`, `ApiVersion`, `ApiDeployment`, `ApiEnvironment`, `SearchResult<T>`, `ChatMessage`, `ChatSession`, `User`, `PaginatedResponse<T>`
- **DTOs**: `ApiCatalogResponse`, `ApiDetailResponse`, `SearchRequest`/`SearchResponse`, `ChatRequest`/`ChatResponse` — `ApiCatalogItem` uses `ApiKind`/`ApiLifecycle` enum types for end-to-end type safety
- **Errors**: `AppError` class with `code`/`statusCode`/`details` + `ErrorCode` enum covering client, server, and domain-specific codes

### Utilities
- 11 type guards for runtime validation of API responses — each guard validates all required fields, uses enum guards (`isApiKind`, `isApiLifecycle`, `isErrorCode`) for enum fields, validates timestamps (`createdAt`/`updatedAt`), and composite guards (`isSearchResult`, `isPaginatedResponse`) validate structural properties and apply the optional `itemGuard` parameter for item-level validation
- Formatters: `formatDate`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatBytes`, `normalizeUrl`, `truncate` (with safe handling for `maxLength <= 0`)
- `toApiCatalogItem()` transformer from full `ApiDefinition` to summary DTO

### Tests
- 93 tests across 3 suites covering all type guards (including negative cases for missing fields, invalid enums, malformed nested structures, and item guard validation), formatters (including edge cases), `AppError`, and `toApiCatalogItem`

```typescript
import { ApiKind, isApiDefinition, formatBytes, AppError, ErrorCode } from '@apic-vibe-portal/shared';
```

### Notable TS 6.0 decisions
- `tsconfig.cjs.json` uses `moduleResolution: "node10"` + `ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"` (required for CJS emit)
- Test tsconfig similarly accommodates ts-jest 29.x which doesn't yet support `bundler` resolution

author: eronfan
body:
## Problem

When configuring MCP servers with `type: "streamable-http"` (e.g. Zhipu BigModel), OpenClaw fails to connect because the required `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` header is not sent.

Server response without the header:
```
"Accept header must include both application/json and text/event-stream"
```

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/mcp-transport.ts`, the `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` was initialized with only user-provided headers (e.g. `Authorization`) but the critical `Accept` header required by the MCP Streamable HTTP spec was not included.

## Fix

Explicitly set `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` in the `requestInit` headers when creating the `StreamableHTTPClientTransport`, merging with any user-provided headers.

## Testing

`pnpm test src/agents/mcp-transport-config.test.ts` passes.

## Issue

Fixes #66940

author: gcappon
body:
Adds two new external forcing inputs to both the multi-meal and single-meal T1D physiological models, enabling clamp-study and IV-delivery scenarios:

- forcing_ra (mg/kg/min): glucose infusion rate added directly to the plasma glucose compartment G (numerator term +forcing_ra/VG).
- forcing_ip (pmol/kg): extra plasma insulin added inside the (Ip[t] - Ipb) drive of the remote insulin action compartment X, i.e. X[t] = (...p2*(SI/VI)*(Ip[t] - Ipb + forcing_ip)...).

Both inputs default to zero so all existing call sites are unaffected. Data classes expose __forcing_input_setup() which initialises the zero arrays; callers can overwrite them before simulation.

## Summary

- Fix RedPanda OOM crash loop on multi-core servers by adding `--smp=1 --memory=1536M` flags and raising Docker memory limit to 4GB
- Add `REDPANDA_KAFKA_PUBLIC_URL` and `REDPANDA_SCHEMA_REGISTRY_PUBLIC_URL` to Infisical secrets for external client configuration

RedPanda auto-detects all 8 host CPUs and allocates memory per-shard. With the 2GB Docker limit, only 464MB was available after 1.5GB reserved, causing `Failed to allocate 8877856 bytes` and exit code 133 crash loop. This made the SASL background config job fail, taking down the entire Spin Up workflow.

author: hongmingwang-rabbit
body:
## Summary
Discovered via deep workspace inspection during a maintenance cycle: every audit cron in molecule-dev was structurally broken. Security Auditor / UIUX Designer / QA Engineer would correctly try to deliver their hourly \`audit_summary\` to PM (per #50 + #75), the platform A2A proxy would reject it with **'access denied: workspaces cannot communicate per hierarchy'**, and the agent would silently fall back to delegating to its direct parent (Dev Lead). PM's category_routing dispatcher was never reached.

## Live evidence (just now)

**From Security Auditor's memory:**
\`\`\`
Conversation: Delegation results are ready. Review them and take appropriate action:
- [failed] Delegating to f3531ba4-d5b2-49c6-b312-950413706e45
  Error: access denied: workspaces cannot communicate per hierarchy
\`\`\`
(\`f3531ba4...\` is PM's workspace ID. Security Auditor's parent is Dev Lead.)

**From Security Auditor's recent activity log:**
\`\`\`
2026-04-15T05:13:07 a2a_send  ok  Delegating to Backend Engineer
2026-04-15T05:12:25 a2a_send  ok  Delegating to Dev Lead
2026-04-15T03:51:15 a2a_send  ok  Delegating to Dev Lead
\`\`\`
Every fall-back delegation went to Dev Lead instead of PM. PM's inbox shows zero \`audit_summary\` deliveries this entire session.

## Root cause
\`registry.CanCommunicate()\` only allowed: self → self, siblings, root-level siblings, **direct** parent ↔ child. A grandchild → grandparent (Security Auditor → Dev Lead → PM) was rejected. The original design wanted strict hierarchy to prevent rogue horizontal A2A — but it also broke the leadership-chain pattern that any audit/escalation flow needs.

## Fix
Generalise to **ancestor ↔ descendant**. Any workspace can talk to any ancestor (any depth) and any descendant (any depth). Direct parent/child remains a fast path that avoids the walk; sibling rules unchanged; cross-subtree A2A still rejected.

Implementation: \`isAncestorOf(ancestorID, childID)\` walks the parent chain in Go with a \`maxAncestorWalk=32\` safety cap so a malformed cycle in the workspaces table cannot loop forever. One DB lookup per step. For a typical 3-deep tree this adds 1-2 extra lookups beyond the direct-parent fast path. Could be optimised to a single recursive CTE later if profiling shows it matters.

## Tests (13 total, all passing)

| Test | Behaviour | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SameWorkspace | self ↔ self | unchanged |
| Siblings | same parent | unchanged |
| RootSiblings | both root | unchanged |
| ParentToChild | direct | unchanged (fast path) |
| ChildToParent | direct | unchanged (fast path) |
| **Allowed_GrandparentToGrandchild** | **NEW** — PM → BE | ✅ |
| **Allowed_GrandchildToGrandparent** | **NEW** — Security Auditor → PM (the actual bug) | ✅ |
| **Allowed_DeepAncestor** | **NEW** — 4-level chain | ✅ |
| **Denied_UnrelatedAncestors** | **NEW** — cross-subtree walks terminate denied | ✅ |
| Denied_DifferentParents | unrelated pairs (extended with walk-lookup mocks) | unchanged behaviour |
| Denied_CousinToRoot | extended walk mocks | unchanged behaviour |
| Denied_CallerNotFound | DB error fail-secure | unchanged |
| Denied_TargetNotFound | DB error fail-secure | unchanged |

The previous \`Denied_Grandchild\` test (which asserted the wrong behaviour) was REPLACED.

## Local verification
\`\`\`
ok  github.com/Molecule-AI/molecule-monorepo/platform/internal/registry  0.005s  (13 tests)
\`\`\`

## Why platform-level
Per the 'platform-wide fixes are mine to ship' rule. Every org template hits the same broken audit-routing chain — fixing it at the platform benefits all users, not just molecule-dev. This unblocks **#50** (PM dispatcher prompt) and **#75** (category_routing) which both assumed audit_summary delivery worked.

## Applied locally
Per the apply-locally rule, I'm rebuilding + force-recreating the platform container in parallel with this PR. Within ~2 min the live system will accept Security Auditor → PM, and the next hourly security audit (next fire 05:17 UTC, +5 min) will deliver its first audit_summary to PM successfully.

## Related
- **#50** PM dispatcher prompt — receiver-side; was waiting for this
- **#75** category_routing — declarative routing; was waiting for this
- **#85** scheduler-died — discovered while debugging this same audit chain
- **#92** systemic supervisor — same investigation arc

author: iliapolo
body:
### Description of changes

This PR improves the snapshot sanitization and normalization pipeline for the gen2 migration e2e system. The main goal is to make snapshots as stable as possible so that rerunning them produces the minimal
amount of changes.

> Example future PR: https://github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-cli/pull/14783

#### Normalization

A new normalize step was added that runs before sanitization. It replaces run-specific values (random env names, CFN stack hashes) in both file content and filenames with deterministic placeholders,
keeping snapshot filenames stable across runs.

#### Sandbox identifier

The sandbox deployment now uses `--identifier e2e` for a deterministic stack name prefix instead of the OS username.

## Summary
PR 2 of Feature 6 — Persistent Webhooks. Implements **Task 4** from [spec §6 Phase 1](docs/feature-6-spec.md). Depends on PR #63 (now merged).

## Changes
- **`jose`** installed for JWKS-based JWT verification (Supabase's modern ES256 flow)
- **`src/middlewares/auth.ts`** — `authMiddleware`:
  - Lazy `createRemoteJWKSet(SUPABASE_JWKS_URL)` so tests can avoid the network
  - `jwtVerify` enforces `iss === SUPABASE_URL`, `aud === "authenticated"`
  - On valid token → auto-upserts `User` row via Prisma singleton from PR 1 (`sub` → `id`, `email` → `email`), attaches `req.userId` + `req.userEmail`
  - 401 on missing Authorization / non-Bearer / empty token / signature failure / missing claims
- **Express `Request` augmentation** for `userId` + `userEmail` (module-wide)
- **`__setVerifyOverrideForTests`** — test-only injection point so unit tests don't hit Supabase
- **7 unit tests** covering every failure path + the happy path

## Out of scope (spec §7)
- Applying middleware to routes — lands with PR 4 (`/api/alerts`) and PR 5 (`/api/webhook`)
- WebSocket JWT handshake — lands with PR 3 (FE auth)
- Rate limiting per user — deferred (non-goal §8)

## Verification (spec §10)
- [x] `cd apps/api-server && npx tsc --noEmit` — passed
- [x] `cd apps/web && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vite build` — passed
- [x] Unit tests: **35/35** passing (7 new auth tests + 28 existing)
  - Local run used the same env vars CI sets, including `SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_JWKS_URL` placeholders
- [x] Rebased on `origin/main`, 0 conflicts, 1 commit

## Notes
- JWKS fetch happens lazily on first real request — server startup stays fast; `jose` caches keys internally and handles rotation
- The `Request.userId` type lives in `middlewares/auth.ts`; any file that imports it gets the augmentation. If that feels too implicit, happy to move it to a dedicated `src/types/express.d.ts` in a follow-up

author: copilot
body:
Adds `install.sh` — a one-stop idempotent installer that sets up the full dotfiles environment from a single command.

### Changes

- **`install.sh`** — installs oh-my-zsh and GNU Stow if missing, backs up conflicting dotfiles to `~/.dotfiles_backup` (with interactive prompt), symlinks everything via `stow --restow`, and creates `~/.zsh_extra`
- **`.stow-local-ignore`** — excludes non-dotfile files (`README.md`, `install.sh`, `.git`, etc.) from stow linking
- **`README.md`** — documents quick start, managed files, and `.zsh_extra` usage

### Usage

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hyunhwan-bcm/dotfiles.git ~/dotfiles
cd ~/dotfiles
./install.sh
```

### Design notes

- Conflict detection handles both real files and symlinks pointing outside the repo (via `readlink -f` comparison)
- Non-interactive mode (CI/piped stdin) auto-accepts backup; interactive mode prompts
- Stow package manager detection covers `apt`, `brew`, `dnf`, `pacman`
- `set -euo pipefail` with explicit error messages on stow failure

author: e7h4n
body:
## Summary

- Replace timer-based `setLoop` polling with Ably-driven realtime push notifications for run events, task list, and voice chat
- Server publishes lightweight invalidation signals to per-user Ably channels (`user:{userId}`); frontend subscribes and re-fetches data through existing ccstate signals
- Falls back to `setLoop` when Ably is unavailable or in test environment — all 1773 existing tests pass without modification

## Architecture

```
Server event → publishUserSignal([userId], topic) → Ably channel user:{userId}
                                                           ↓
Frontend ablyNotify(topic, body, interval, signal) ← subscribes to topic
                                                           ↓
                                                   Executes body (same as setLoop body)
                                                           ↓
                                               Ably unavailable → fallback to setLoop
```

### Topics
| Topic | Trigger | Audience |
|---|---|---|
| `thread:{runId}` | Run events written, run complete/fail/cancel | Run owner |
| `tasks:{orgId}` | Task archive/unarchive, run terminal state | Org members |
| `voice:{sessionId}` | Voice chat context append | Session user |
| `voice:prep` | Voice chat preparation ready | Preparation owner |

### Key design decisions
- **Invalidation-only signals** — Ably messages carry no data; frontend re-fetches via existing HTTP endpoints
- **Per-user channels** — Each user subscribes to `user:{userId}` only; server computes audience per event
- **Token security** — Token endpoint only grants `subscribe` permission on user's own channel
- **Non-blocking publishing** — All server-side publish calls use `after()` to avoid adding latency to responses

## Changes

### Server-side (6 files)
- `realtime/client.ts` — Add `publishUserSignal()`, `generatePlatformUserToken()`
- `realtime/audience.ts` — Add `getOrgMemberUserIds()` (new)
- `zero/realtime/token/route.ts` — Platform token endpoint (new)
- Webhook complete/events/cancel routes — Publish run & task signals
- Tasks route — Publish task list signals
- Voice chat routes — Publish voice context & preparation signals

### Frontend (10 files)
- `realtime.ts` — Ably client singleton + `ablyNotify$` computed (new)
- `bootstrap.ts` — Initialize Ably after Clerk auth
- 8 files replacing `setLoop` → `ablyNotify` (11 call sites total)

### Contract
- `@vm0/core` — Add `platformRealtimeTokenContract`

## Test plan

- [x] All 1773 existing tests pass (ablyNotify automatically falls back to setLoop in VITEST)
- [x] Type check passes across all packages
- [x] Lint passes (0 errors)
- [x] Knip passes (no unused exports)
- [ ] Manual test: verify Ably connection establishes on app load
- [ ] Manual test: verify run events update in real-time without polling delay
- [ ] Manual test: verify task list updates when another user archives a task
- [ ] Manual test: verify graceful fallback when ABLY_API_KEY is not configured

author: ebeneezer
body:
### 🎯 What
Fixed a buffer overflow vulnerability in `mrmac/mrmac.c` by replacing a dangerous `strcpy` call with `strncpy` and ensuring explicit null termination.

### ⚠️ Risk
The use of `strcpy` to copy variable names into a fixed-size buffer could lead to a buffer overflow if a name longer than `MAX_SYMBOL_NAME` was provided (though checked earlier, defense-in-depth is required). An attacker could potentially exploit this to cause a crash or execute arbitrary code.

### 🛡️ Solution
Replaced `strcpy(g_symbols[g_symbol_count].name, name);` with:
```c
strncpy(g_symbols[g_symbol_count].name, name, MAX_SYMBOL_NAME);
g_symbols[g_symbol_count].name[MAX_SYMBOL_NAME] = '\0';
```
This follows the established pattern in the codebase for safe string handling and ensures the buffer is never exceeded, regardless of the input length. Verified that `g_symbols[g_symbol_count].name` has size `MAX_SYMBOL_NAME + 1`, thus no off-by-one error was introduced.

Verified by successfully building `mrmac/mrmac.o` and running the full regression test suite (`make regression-check-core`), with all tests passing.
