author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Fixes the failing [Dependency Updates workflow](https://github.com/JerrettDavis/MillProbeStudio/actions/runs/21131516515).

## Root Cause

The workflow was structured as:
1. `npm update` — installs and updates packages + lock file
2. `npm ci` — strict clean install from updated lock file ← **this failed**

`npm update` upgraded `@semantic-release/github` to v11.x (which requires `semantic-release@>=24`), while the lock file still held `semantic-release@21`. The subsequent `npm ci` then failed with an `ERESOLVE` peer dependency conflict.

## Fix

Restructured the steps into the correct order:
1. **Install dependencies** (`npm ci`) — clean baseline install from existing lock file
2. **Update dependencies** (`npm update` + `npm audit fix`) — update packages and lock file
3. **Run tests** (`npm run test` + `npm run build`) — validate without a redundant reinstall

This is the standard pattern for dependency update workflows: establish a clean baseline first, then update, then test.

body:
## Bug
On every scan, the scanner generated policies to disk AFTER writing the manifest. \`scanArtifacts\` checked the filesystem during \`scan()\`, BEFORE the files were rendered. So the manifest said \`artifacts: missing\` even though the scanner was about to generate them. The POST sent that stale manifest to the dashboard. Dashboard showed artifacts as missing even when the scanner produced them moments before.

## Fix
- Write manifest LAST, after all policy files have been written to disk
- Explicitly set \`manifest.artifacts\` to \`generated/present\` after rendering — the scanner just wrote them, so the manifest should say they're there

## Check Production gets more thorough
Previously only updated security headers and HTTPS enforcement.

Now it ALSO:
- Fetches \`/privacy-policy\`, \`/terms-of-service\`, \`/vulnerability-disclosure\`, \`/.well-known/security.txt\` on the live site
- Marks each as \`present\` if the URL returns 2xx, otherwise preserves the existing status (doesn't regress)
- Returns per-policy served status in the response

## Verified locally
Wiped \`.grc/\` and \`docs/policies/\` on joeeftekhari.com, ran scanner fresh. Manifest now reports all artifacts as generated/present on the first run.

author: 0-jake-0
body:
## Summary

Introduces a complete `web` adapter for wingfoil that enables bidirectional streaming between a wingfoil graph and one or more browsers over WebSocket. This includes the Rust server implementation, browser client libraries (TypeScript/JavaScript and Python bindings), and comprehensive integration tests.

## Key Changes

### Core Adapter (Rust)
- **`wingfoil/src/adapters/web/`**: New adapter module with:
  - `server.rs`: HTTP + WebSocket server using axum, running on a dedicated tokio runtime with synchronous bind
  - `codec.rs`: Wire codec abstraction supporting bincode (default, compact) and JSON (debug-friendly) formats
  - `write.rs`: `web_pub()` sink for publishing graph values to connected clients
  - `read.rs`: `web_sub()` source for receiving frames from browsers as wingfoil streams
  - `integration_tests.rs`: In-process integration tests using tokio-tungstenite client
  - `mod.rs`: Module re-exports and documentation with usage examples

### Wire Types
- **`wingfoil-wire-types/`**: New crate defining shared `Envelope` and `ControlMessage` types used by both server and browser client, ensuring compile-time wire format compatibility

### Browser Client (TypeScript/JavaScript)
- **`wingfoil-js/`**: Framework-agnostic `WingfoilClient` class with:
  - WebSocket connection management with automatic reconnection
  - Topic subscription/unsubscription with listener dispatch
  - Publish capability for client → server communication
  - Reactive framework bindings for Solid.js, Svelte, and Vue 3
  - Example Solid.js dashboard application

### WebAssembly Codec
- **`wingfoil-wasm/`**: Rust-to-WebAssembly codec compiled via wasm-pack, providing:
  - Envelope encoding/decoding matching the server's wire format
  - Control message encoding (subscribe/unsubscribe)
  - Payload serialization for both bincode and JSON codecs
  - Consumed by `@wingfoil/client` npm package

### Python Bindings
- **`wingfoil-python/src/py_web.rs`**: Python API for `WebServer` with:
  - Server construction and configuration (codec, static file serving)
  - `web_pub()` and `web_sub()` stream methods
  - Integration with existing Python stream operators
- **`wingfoil-python/tests/test_web.py`**: Integration tests using raw WebSocket protocol

### CI/CD
- **`.github/workflows/web-integration.yml`**: New workflow for:
  - Rust integration tests (in-process, no external services)
  - wingfoil-wasm build and unit tests
  - JavaScript/TypeScript tests

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Synchronous bind**: TCP port binding happens synchronously in the builder so port conflicts surface before the graph starts, matching the pattern used by PrometheusExporter
- **Dedicated runtime**: HTTP server runs on its own current-thread tokio runtime in a spawned thread, isolating it from the graph's async context
- **Lossy broadcast**: Per-topic broadcast channels with bounded capacity; slow consumers receive `RecvError::Lagged` instead of blocking the graph
- **Bounded queues**: Per-connection outbound queues and per-topic mpsc channels prevent misbehaving clients from growing memory unbounded
- **Single source of truth**: Wire types live in `wingfoil-wire-types` so server and wasm client cannot drift; wire mismatches become compile errors
- **Historical mode support**: Server can be created as a no-op for `RunMode::HistoricalFrom` runs via `start_historical()`
- **Static file serving**: Optional `tower-http::services::ServeDir` integration for hosting UI bundles on the same origin as the WebSocket endpoint

author: ajaythorve
body:
## Summary

- **server.js**: Remove the overly strict `expiresAt` gate from `extractIdTokenFromSession` — sending an expired idToken is better than sending nothing. The backend can still identify the caller, and the session refreshes within seconds of page load.
- **use-websocket-chat.ts**: Add a token-refresh-aware reconnect effect that watches `idToken` from `useAuth()`. When the token rotates (session refresh picks up new credentials from Starfleet), forces a WebSocket disconnect/reconnect so `server.js` decodes the fresh session JWT. Defers during streaming, loading, or pending HITL interactions.

Fixes the "UI stops responding after a few hours / page reopen" issue where users had to logout/login or clear cache to recover.

### Root cause

When a page is reopened after hours, the session JWT cookie still exists (24h maxAge) but the OAuth `expiresAt` inside it is stale. The WebSocket connects before the `SessionProvider` refreshes the token, and `extractIdTokenFromSession` rejects the expired token — sending **no auth** to the backend. ECI and other auth-gated services fail silently. There was also no mechanism to reconnect the WebSocket after the session refreshed.

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles clean (`tsc --noEmit`)
- [x] All 39 existing tests pass (29 websocket-chat + 10 connection-recovery)
- [ ] Manual: open app, wait for token refresh (~55 min or adjust `TOKEN_REFRESH_BUFFER_MINUTES`), verify console shows `[WS] Token refreshed — reconnecting for fresh auth`
- [ ] Manual: close tab, wait >1 hour, reopen — verify app works immediately without logout/login
- [ ] Manual: trigger HITL prompt, wait for token refresh, verify reconnect defers until HITL completes

author: siddseethepalli
body:
## Summary
Fixes 3 correctness gaps in wakeAgentForOpportunity identified during plan review.

1. **Client event translation**: wake no longer emits raw AgentEvents as ServerMessages. Events are translated via the canonical handler so clients receive correctly-shaped 'assistant_text_delta'/'message_complete' frames with conversationId.
2. **Full tail persistence**: wake now persists every message produced by the agent loop (assistant messages + tool_result user messages), not just the first assistant message. Prevents DB/history desync when the wake produces tool calls.
3. **Processing guard**: wake marks conversation.processing during the agent loop so concurrent user turns can't race and produce interleaved history.

Part of plan review for meet-phase-2-chat.md.

author: sbc100
body:
Introduce PThread.terminateRuntime which is called during runtime exit. This function not only terminates all workers but also clears the thread state of the main thread and sends a final notification to its mailbox.

By clearing the thread state, _pthread_self() will now return 0, which causes the mailbox checking loop to terminate instead of re-registering a new Atomics.waitAsync promise. This allows the Wasm memory and module instance to be garbage collected.

Fixes: #20920

author: copilot
body:
With `cell_size == step_size` (15 m) the A* grid was too coarse to distinguish free road corridors from obstacle interiors — the only traversable path was the city perimeter, producing paths ~37% longer than RRT* (2025 m vs 1472 m). Dividing by 5 (1 centre cell + 2σ margin each side) gives 3 m cells that fit inside 30 m corridors with margin to spare.

## Changes

- **`sparse.py` — `_coerce_astar_cell_size`**: default changed from `step_size` → `step_size / 5`; accepts an optional explicit `cell_size` override so the YAML value takes precedence.
  ```python
  # Before
  def _coerce_astar_cell_size(step_size) -> float: ...  # returned step_size[0]

  # After
  def _coerce_astar_cell_size(step_size, cell_size=None) -> float: ...
  # returns cell_size if provided, else step_size[0] / 5
  ```

- **`sparse.py` — `CityScene.build()`**: passes `cfg.get("astar_cell_size")` as the override, wiring the new YAML key into the grid construction.

- **`city.yml`**: adds `astar_cell_size: 3.0  # [m]` to the `planner` section, making cell size a first-class tunable parameter alongside `step_size`.

- **`tests/tools/test_astar_cell_size.py`**: 10 new tests covering scalar/sequence/ndarray defaults, explicit override, `None` fallback, empty-sequence guard, and the city.yml invariant (`astar_cell_size == step_size[0] / 5`).

pr: #49034

PR #48890 introduced a pathless "summary placeholder" in SegmentInfo.Deltalogs for V3 manifest segments so that compaction triggers keep working. On the segment loader side, however, the path-based V1 delta download loop still runs over these placeholders: DecompressBinLog rebuilds a V1-style LogPath from the LogID, and the loader issues MultiRead on a path that does not exist for V3 segments (real delta data lives under {basePath}/_delta/ via manifest), making V3 segments with deltas fail to load.

Skip the V1 download loop when loadInfo.ManifestPath is set; the manifest-based reader (NewDeltalogReaderFromManifest) already handles V3 delta loading a few lines below. The rowNums preallocation still benefits from the placeholder's EntriesNum.

Added two focused tests under SegmentLoaderSuite:
- V3 placeholder -> legacy reader not called, manifest reader called
- V1 intact     -> legacy reader called, manifest reader not called

- Enforce a new documentation rule requiring comments on every function and major processing block to improve maintainability. 
- Support NuGet-style dependencies in project manifests so `version` entries in `[dependencies]` can be interpreted as NuGet packages. 
- Provide deterministic dependency resolution, clearer diagnostics for conflicts/cycles/missing packages, and optional automatic restore support.

### Description
- Update `AGENTS.md` to require comments for every function and each major processing block and update `PLANS.md` with tasks for adding block comments and NuGet resolution work. 
- Extend `src/Atla.Build/Build.fs` with manifest parsing helpers (`tryGetRequiredString`, `parseDependencies`, `parseManifest`), added block comments, and the `buildProject` entry that uses `Resolver.resolveDependencies`. 
- Implement `src/Atla.Build/Resolver.fs` enhancements: introduce `DependencySpec` with `NuGetDependency`, `Manifest` type, `getNuGetPackagesRoot`, `tryRunRestore` which runs `dotnet restore`, `tryResolveNuGetDependency` to check cache and optionally restore, and an improved `resolveDependencies` that performs DFS, cycle detection, version/duplicate-source diagnostics, and returns a deterministic sorted list of `ResolvedDependency`. 
- Add inline block comments describing behavior and decisions around manifest normalization, NuGet cache lookup, auto-restore control via `ATLA_BUILD_ENABLE_NUGET_RESTORE`, and resolution ordering.

### Testing
- Ran the full test suite with `dotnet test` and confirmed no regressions and all tests passed. 
- Ran `Atla.Build.Tests` to exercise manifest parsing and dependency resolution scenarios (path, NuGet, cache/missing and conflict cases) and observed expected pass results.

## Summary
- QA 리포트: 1년 운세의 오행(목/화/토/금/수) 비율이 사용자 실제 사주와 다르게 나오는 버그 (목 약·화 강 사주인데 목이 강하게 노출)
- 원인: 서버가 오행 분석을 Gemini에 전적으로 위임하면서 프롬프트가 너무 얇아, LLM이 사주 원국을 계산하지 않고 요청 연도 분위기로 비율을 찍어버림
- 조치: \`GeminiService.toYearlyFortunePrompt()\` 프롬프트 전면 개편

## 프롬프트 주요 변경점
1. **원국 계산 강제** — 연주·월주·일주·시주를 먼저 세우도록 절차화하고, 천간/지지 본기 오행 매핑 테이블을 프롬프트에 명시
2. **\`percentage\` 정의 고정** — "원국 기준 오행 비율(합 100±2)"로 못 박음
3. **\`status\` 산출 규칙** — 원국+세운 합산 후 \`≥30% EXCESS / ≤10% DEFICIENT / 그 외 BALANCED\`, 상생/상극 조정 규칙 포함
4. **이번 버그 직접 차단** — "요청 연도가 2026이니 화가 강할 것 같다 식 추측 금지", "일간이 목이라고 목이 많은 게 아니다" 경고 명시
5. **결정론 요구** — 같은 생년월일시 입력은 항상 같은 원국
6. **\`birthTime\` null 처리** — 기존엔 \`null\` 문자열이 프롬프트에 박혔음. \`?: "모름"\` 분기 + 시주 제외 6글자 기준 처리

## 한계 (후속 작업 후보)
프롬프트 보강은 응급 처치. LLM의 만세력 암기 정확도는 여전히 불안정하므로, 재발 시 **서버에서 사주 원국을 직접 계산**해 프롬프트에 주입하고 Gemini는 해석 텍스트만 생성하도록 하는 B안이 필요.

body:
## Summary
This PR converts all I/O-bound operations to async/await, improving scalability
by freeing threads during blocking operations instead of holding them idle.

## Problem
The current implementation blocks threads during I/O.
In a high-throughput scenario, this exhausts the thread pool and limits 
concurrent request handling.

## Solution
Convert to async/await.

## Naming Convention
Following .NET conventions:
- Async methods suffixed with `Async`
- Return `Task` (void) or `Task<T>` (with result)
- `CancellationToken` parameter (added for future extensibility)

## Testing
- [x] Application runs with async Main
- [x] Orders save successfully
- [x] Product lookup works with simulated delay
- [x] No deadlocks or race conditions

author: werb210
body:
### Motivation
- Tests were failing due to a module-level `Set` that persisted mounted routes across app instances and caused `ROUTE COLLISION` errors.
- Multiple app instances in the same test run must not share mount state so tests can register routes independently.
- There were duplicate root (`"/"`) mounts (two routers mounted at the same path) which risked collisions and non-deterministic behavior.

### Description
- Replaced the global mount state with a factory `createMountTracker()` in `src/routes/_canonicalMount.ts` which returns a `mount` closure that keeps per-instance state.
- Updated `src/routes/routeRegistry.ts` to import `createMountTracker` and call `const mount = createMountTracker();` inside `registerApiRouteMounts()` so each registration gets isolated mount tracking.
- Consolidated duplicate root mounts by composing `readinessRoutes` and `signnowRoutes` into a single `rootRoutes` and mounting `"/"` only once in `API_ROUTE_MOUNTS`.
- Removed the previous `resetMountedRoutes()` usage and replaced global-reset semantics with per-registration trackers to avoid global state leakage.

### Testing
- Ran the test suite with `npm test` and it passed: `Test Files 28 passed (28)` and `Tests 66 passed (66)`.
- No `ROUTE COLLISION` errors occurred during the test run and OTP-related tests were no longer prematurely failing due to route collisions.

## Summary - Narrow `(s) => s` full-store subscriptions to specific field selectors in `contextPanelStore` and `credenzaStore` - `InfoContent`: selects `infoContent`, `pageActions`, `pageViewSwitch` only - `ContextPanelInner`: selects `activeTabId`, `dynamicTabs` only - `GlobalContextPanel`: selects `isOpen` only - `GlobalCredenza`: selects `stack` only ## Test plan - [ ] Open/close context panel — no unrelated re-renders - [ ] Switch context panel tabs — only `ContextPanelInner` re-renders - [ ] Open/close credenza — only `GlobalCredenza` re-renders 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Reduzimos re-renderizações desnecessárias ao trocar assinaturas `(s) => s` por seletores específicos em `useStore`, melhorando a performance do painel de contexto e da credenza. - **Refactors** - `InfoContent`: agora assina apenas `infoContent`, `pageActions`, `pageViewSwitch` de `contextPanelStore`. - `ContextPanelInner`: agora assina apenas `activeTabId`, `dynamicTabs` de `contextPanelStore`. - `GlobalContextPanel`: agora assina apenas `isOpen` de `contextPanelStore`. - `GlobalCredenza`: agora assina apenas `stack` de `credenzaStore`. Written for commit 502d40da8c7c2ae3cfae6c739a6ebb5136a00dca. Summary will update on new commits. Review in cubic

Greptile Summary

O PR tem o objetivo correto — estreitar os seletores do `useStore` para evitar re-renders desnecessários — mas a implementação em `InfoContent` e `ContextPanelInner` é incorreta. `useStore` do `@tanstack/react-store` usa igualdade referencial (`Object.is`); seletores que retornam objetos literais criam uma nova referência a cada chamada, fazendo o componente re-renderizar em **todo** update da store, equivalente ou pior que o `(s) => s` original. - Os seletores de primitivo em `GlobalContextPanel` (`s.isOpen`) e `GlobalCredenza` (`s.stack`) estão corretos. - `InfoContent` e `ContextPanelInner` precisam ser reescritos com chamadas individuais de `useStore` por campo.

Confidence Score: 3/5

O PR não deve ser mergeado: a otimização central falha em 2 dos 4 componentes. Dois P1 ativos — seletores com objeto literal sempre produzem nova referência com Object.is, anulando o objetivo do PR em InfoContent e ContextPanelInner. apps/web/src/features/context-panel/context-panel.tsx

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/web/src/features/context-panel/context-panel.tsx | Os seletores de `InfoContent` e `ContextPanelInner` retornam objetos literais a cada chamada, invalidando a otimização pretendida; os seletores de primitivo em `GlobalContextPanel` estão corretos. | | apps/web/src/hooks/use-credenza.tsx | Seletor correto: retorna diretamente a referência do array `s.stack`, que só muda quando a store é mutada. |

Flowchart

```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart TD subgraph Store["contextPanelStore / credenzaStore"] S[Estado atualizado via setState] end subgraph Correto["Seletores corretos"] GCP["GlobalContextPanel\nuseStore(s => s.isOpen)"] GC["GlobalCredenza\nuseStore(s => s.stack)"] end subgraph Incorreto["Objeto literal - sempre nova referencia"] IC["InfoContent\n(s) => ({ infoContent, pageActions, pageViewSwitch })"] CPI["ContextPanelInner\n(s) => ({ activeTabId, dynamicTabs })"] end S -->|"Object.is OK"| GCP S -->|"Object.is OK"| GC S -->|"SEMPRE re-render"| IC S -->|"SEMPRE re-render"| CPI ```

author: paden
body:
## What
Three defensive layers against silent scheduler hot-loops:
1. **Write-time coercion** (`coerceScript` in `src/db.ts`) — stringifies Buffers/numbers before insert in `createTask`/`updateTask` so the `script` column is always `text | null`.
2. **Startup repair** (`castNonTextScripts`) — during scheduler lint, CASTs any pre-existing non-text `script` rows to TEXT and logs each fix.
3. **Outer try/catch in `runTask`** — records failures via `logTaskRun` and advances `next_run` (with a +5m fallback if `computeNextRun` itself throws), so any future unhandled throw surfaces in task history instead of pegging the loop.

## Why
`task-1775619472081-ja2ron` (panda reveal poller) was silently hot-looping: its `script` column had been stored as a BLOB, so `script.trim()` in `runTask` threw `TypeError` on every tick. The inner try/catch sat too deep — the throw escaped before `logTaskRun` and `updateTaskAfterRun` could run, so `next_run` never advanced. The scheduler re-picked the task on every poll, and the only trace was a stderr line in `nanoclaw.error.log` (never `nanoclaw.log`).

The immediate row was already CAST'd manually. These layers prevent the class of bug: corrupted column state at rest, future throws from any other cause, and new BLOBs sneaking in through write paths.

## How
- `src/db.ts`: new `coerceScript(value: unknown): string | null`, applied in `createTask` line 543 and `updateTask` line 596. New `castNonTextScripts(): string[]` that uses `typeof(script) NOT IN ('text', 'null')` with a transaction-wrapped CAST.
- `src/task-scheduler.ts`: body of `runTask` (post the invalid-folder early-return) wrapped in outer `try { ... } catch (err) { logger.error + logTaskRun + updateTaskAfterRun }`. `lintScheduledTasks` now calls `castNonTextScripts` and logs each repair as WARN. Export `_runTaskForTests = runTask` for regression test.

## Testing
- `npm run build` — clean

author: tmokenc
body:
This PR adds support for per-level alphabets in `mata::nft::Nft`.

The main addition is:

- `std::vector<Alphabet*> level_alphabets`

with the following semantics:

- in case the vector is empty, `Nft` can fallback to use the inherited `nfa::Nfa::alphabet`
- if different levels use different alphabets, `Nft::alphabet` is set to `nullptr`, and the per-level alphabets are stored in `level_alphabets`
- When all levels share the same alphabet, Nft can still expose a shared alphabet through the inherited Nfa::Nfa field. (not sure if this is necessary)

The PR also adds two helper functions:

- `alphabet_of_level` returns the alphabet for a given level and falls back to the inherited `Nfa` alphabet when no level-specific alphabet is available
- `set_level_alphabets` to assign or update alphabets

This PR does not yet introduce any changes to NFT operations or to the `.mata` format for NFTs. The `.mata` format part likely deserves a separate discussion.

## Summary
This PR introduces four new specialized UI components to replace simple textarea inputs for key habit-building steps. Each component provides a more guided, interactive experience with pre-built suggestions, toggles, and structured data capture.

## Key Changes

### New Step Types & Components
- **Distraction Board** (`distraction-board`): Replace textarea with an interactive list where users can add distractions from suggestions or manually, then assign tactics (Remove, Block, Mute, Hide, Relocate) to each one
- **Friction Reducer** (`friction-reducer`): Replace textarea with toggleable cards for six friction-reduction tactics (Prepare, Cue, Stack, Shrink, Default, Commit), each with optional detail textarea
- **Scenario Plans** (`scenario-plans`): Replace textarea with a grid of scenario cards (Sick, Travelling, Exhausted, Busy, Weather, Low Mood) where users define fallback actions, with a reminder of their normal SSMART plan
- **Missed-Day Plan** (`missed-day-plan`): Replace textarea with two sections: self-forgiveness mantras (with pre-written suggestions) and a restart plan (with auto-suggestion from SSMART)

### Data Structure Updates
- Added `suggestions`, `tactics`, `scenarios`, and `mantras` arrays to step definitions
- Implemented specialized empty state generators for each new type
- Updated `isStepEmpty()` validation logic to handle structured data formats
- Enhanced `persistCurrentInputs()` to extract data from new component types

### Rendering & Interaction
- Added `renderDistractionBoard()`, `renderFrictionReducer()`, `renderScenarioPlans()`, `renderMissedDayPlan()` functions
- Added corresponding wire functions for event delegation and state management
- Implemented suggestion chips, toggle buttons, and pre-filled options
- Added focus management and re-render logic for dynamic list operations

### Report Generation
- Updated report generation to handle structured types and display them appropriately
- Added `structuredTypes` set to identify which steps contain complex data
- Implemented custom rendering for each new type in the report output

### Styling
- Added comprehensive CSS for all four new components with consistent design language
- Implemented responsive grid layouts (2-column on desktop, 1-column on mobile)
- Added visual feedback for selected states, hover effects, and focus states
- Used existing color variables (terra, teal, gold) for visual hierarchy

## Notable Implementation Details
- Distraction rows support dynamic add/remove with automatic list re-rendering
- Friction cards show/hide detail textareas based on toggle state
- Scenario cards highlight when filled and show a contextual reminder of the user's normal habit
- Missed-day plan syncs between pre-written mantra buttons and the textarea
- All components preserve user input during interactions and properly sync state with the answers object

author: paynejd
body:
## Summary

Sets `num_returned` on the `MetadataToConceptsListView` (`$match`) response so the analytics middleware records the total matched-item count as `APITransaction.item_count`. Before this fix, every `$match` transaction recorded `item_count=0` because the POST returned directly without going through the list mixin that normally sets the header.

Closes OpenConceptLab/ocl_online#73.

## Changes

```python
results = self.filter_queryset()
response = Response(results)
# num_returned is picked up by the analytics middleware as
# APITransaction.item_count (see ocl_online#73).
if isinstance(results, list):
    response['num_returned'] = sum(
        len(r.get('results', [])) for r in results if isinstance(r, dict)
    )
return response
```

`filter_queryset` returns a list of `{'row': ..., 'results': [...], ...}` dicts, one per input row. Summing the `results` lengths gives the total items matched across the whole request — the right denominator for "rows matched per request" analysis.

## Scope

**In**: `MetadataToConceptsListView` (`/concepts/$match/`).

**Out**: `RerankConceptsListView` (different semantics), `$match-scispacy-loinc` (lives in separate `ocl-scispacy-loinc` repo), 403 early-return path (`num_returned` stays unset → effectively 0, which is correct).

## Test plan

- [ ] Apply locally, POST `/concepts/$match/` with 5 input rows returning varying match counts
- [ ] Verify response has `num_returned` with the summed count
- [ ] Verify new APITransaction row in staging has `item_count` equal to the header value
- [ ] Regression: confirm body shape unchanged

## Cluster context

This is one of 7 PRs closing out Bundle 2 of the `data-extraction-v2` analytics instrumentation work. Each PR is small and independently mergeable except where noted.

body:
## Summary

Fixes BACKLOG-1627 -- when an iPhone is connected but untrusted, the auto-pair code from BACKLOG-1582 never properly identified trust-related errors, leaving users with a static "Connect Your iPhone" screen and no guidance.

### Three fixes:

1. **Parse trust-specific errors from libimobiledevice stderr** in `deviceDetectionService.ts`
   - Detects `"Password protected (-17)"` (phone locked) and `"Pairing dialog response pending (-19)"` (trust dialog showing)
   - Emits `device-needs-trust` event with typed `reason` field (`"locked"` | `"trust_pending"` | `"unknown"`)

2. **Differentiated user guidance in UI** via `useIPhoneSync.ts`
   - New `mapTrustReasonToGuidance()` maps trust reason to `UserFacingError` with specific messages:
     - Locked: "Unlock your iPhone and tap Trust when prompted"
     - Trust pending: "Tap Trust on your iPhone to allow syncing"
     - Unknown: Generic trust guidance with reconnect suggestion

3. **Polling back-off for trust-pending devices**
   - Trust-pending devices skip `getDeviceInfo` calls for 8 seconds (was 2s every cycle)
   - Reduces log spam and CPU during trust-pending state
   - Back-off state clears on successful connection or disconnect

### Files changed
- `electron/services/deviceDetectionService.ts` -- trust error parsing, back-off, reason in events
- `src/hooks/useIPhoneSync.ts` -- differentiated trust guidance messages
- `src/types/iphone.ts` -- added `TrustErrorReason` shared type
- `electron/handlers/deviceHandlers.ts` -- updated IPC type annotation with reason field
- `electron/preload/deviceBridge.ts` -- updated onNeedsTrust callback type with reason field

Two issues with the deload / rest week modal:

author: funkywhitecat
body:
scripts/qwen_image_mcp.py exposes the Serverless Qwen-Image 2512 endpoint as a single MCP tool, generate_image, callable from any MCP-aware client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, LM Studio, Cursor, Continue, etc.).

- Uses the official Python MCP SDK (pip install "mcp>=1.0") via FastMCP for a minimal-boilerplate server with stdio transport.
- Tool args mirror src/workflows.py's convenience shape: prompt, negative_prompt, seed, width, height, steps, cfg, plus an optional save_path. Defaults are aligned with the worker (1104x1472 portrait, 50 steps, cfg 4.0).
- Validates resolution client-side against the same seven-entry SUPPORTED_RESOLUTIONS list the worker enforces, so bad calls fail fast with a helpful message instead of round-tripping to RunPod for a rejection.
- Returns the PNG twice: once inline as an MCP ImageContent block so vision-capable models can see it in-context, once on disk at ~/qwen_image_output/YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS_<seed>.png (configurable via QWEN_IMAGE_DEFAULT_OUT_DIR) so the artifact outlives the chat turn. LM Studio's MCP client specifically renders inline images in-chat and saves them to its attachment panel, matching this shape.
- Reads RUNPOD_API_KEY + RUNPOD_ENDPOINT_ID from the environment the MCP client hands down (via its mcpServers ... env block), never from on-disk config, so secrets stay in the client's vault.
- Runsync HTTP timeout defaults to 900 s to cover cold worker + warmup + 50-step generation; override with RUNPOD_RUNSYNC_TIMEOUT.
- Module docstring includes copy-pasteable registration snippets for Claude Code (claude mcp add ...), project-local .mcp.json, LM Studio (Settings -> Program -> Integrations -> mcp.json), and Claude Desktop (claude_desktop_config.json).

author: ikeboy003
body:
postgres.js (and likely other drivers) sends Flush between Parse/Describe and Bind/Execute when describeFirst is enabled (the default for parameterized non-prepared queries). pgcat was logging 'Unexpected code: H' and dropping the message, leaving the client hung waiting for the ParameterDescription/RowDescription response that never arrived.

Add a Flush arm that drains the buffered extended-protocol messages into self.buffer (same as Sync), appends the Flush byte, sends to the server, forwards the server response, and keeps the server checked out so the subsequent Bind/Execute/Sync can complete on the same backend.

author: zachfi
body:
## Device Information

- **Device Name:** Razer Seiren V3 Chroma (USB Microphone)
- **VID:PID:** 1532:056F
- **Interface:** HID interface 3 (bInterfaceProtocol=0), 3x UAC2 audio interfaces

Closes #2640
Related: #2479 (Seiren V3 Mini), #1902 (Seiren V2 X), #1669 (Seiren Emote)

## Changes

### driver/razeraccessory_driver.h
- Add `USB_DEVICE_ID_RAZER_SEIREN_V3_CHROMA 0x056F`

### driver/razeraccessory_driver.c
- Add device to all effect switch cases (static, spectrum, wave, breath, none, custom, set_key_row, brightness) using `transaction_id = 0x1F`
- Custom `razer_send_payload` path for the Seiren V3 Chroma (see **Protocol Notes** below)
- `expected_protocol = 0` in probe/remove (bInterfaceProtocol=0)

### daemon/openrazer_daemon/hardware/accessory.py
- Add `RazerSeirenV3Chroma` class
- `MATRIX_DIMS = [1, 1]` — single-zone RGB ring
- `WAVE_DIRS = (1, 2)` and brightness support included

### install_files/udev/99-razer.rules
- Add `056f` to accessory PID list

### README.md
- Add device to supported devices table

### daemon/openrazer_daemon/daemon.py
- Fix `_check_plugdev_group()`: when the plugdev group doesn't exist (e.g. Arch Linux), return `True` rather than falling through to `False`
- Fix device access check: replace hardcoded plugdev group-name assertion with `os.access(test_file, os.R_OK)` to test actual file readability

## Protocol Notes

The Seiren V3 Chroma uses a **non-standard USB protocol** compared to other Razer accessories:

1. **63-byte payload** (vs the standard 90-byte `razer_report`): The HID report descriptor on interface 3 defines a vendor-specific Feature report (ID 7) with 63 bytes. The CRC covers bytes 2–60 and is placed at byte 61 (vs bytes 2–87 at byte 88 for standard devices).

2. **Report ID embedded in data**: The device has no HID Output reports defined in its descriptor. When hidraw sends via `write()`, the kernel's `usbhid_output_report()` includes the report ID (0x07) as the first byte of the USB data buffer (64 bytes total). The driver replicates this by prepending 0x07 and sending 64 bytes via `razer_send_control_msg_old_device()` with `report_value=0x0207` (Output type, ID 7) on USB interface 3.

3. **No GET_REPORT response**: The device does not respond to GET_FEATURE_REPORT, so the driver skips the standard request/response path entirely (send-only).

4. **Transaction ID**: `0x1F` for all effect and brightness commands, confirmed on hardware.

## Hardware Test Results

Tested on Arch Linux, kernel 6.19.11:
- Static color ✓
- Spectrum cycling ✓
- Wave effect ✓
- Breath (single, dual, random) ✓
- Brightness control ✓
- Recognized by openrazer-daemon as `RazerSeirenV3Chroma`
- Controlled via D-Bus from custom widget (static effect across 3 devices simultaneously)

## USB HID Descriptor (interface 3)

```
06 53 FF 09 04 A1 01 85 07 15 00 26 FF 00 09 F0
75 08 95 3F B1 02 09 F1 75 08 95 3F 81 02 85 05
15 00 26 FF 00 09 F2 75 08 95 0F 81 02 C0
```

Vendor collection (0xFF53 / usage 0x04): Report ID 7 = 63-byte Feature + Input report pair.

author: idan-rubin
body:
## Problem
The Prompt and Plan popover buttons were gated behind the \`plan\` SSE event. In the early seconds of a run (and for runs where the plan event hadn't arrived yet) the buttons simply didn't render. User report: "I dont see the prompt and plan buttons at all now."

## Fix
Remove the \`{plan && ...}\` wrapper. Buttons render from the first frame of the running view; when the plan content isn't available yet the popover body shows "Loading…" instead. Prompt popover will also show "Loading…" until the \`plan\` event fires (the prompt lives alongside the plan in that event).

Agent-loop and all backend code untouched — this is a frontend-only fix.

## Test plan
- [x] lint / typecheck / format / build pass
- [ ] Navigate to a run in progress at step 0 (before plan arrives) — both Prompt and Plan buttons are visible
- [ ] Click either → popover opens showing "Loading…"; once plan arrives, popovers populate
- [ ] Click outside or press Escape → popover closes
